Wave energy from the tsunami reached the West Coast and caused approximately $6.5 million in damage to Santa Cruz Harbor, according to the local Port Director. Damage was inflicted on utility infrastructure, pilings and bathroom facilities, as more than 3 feet of water poured in. Waves also knocked out power around the harbor docks, a place where many people live on their boats.||https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2022/01/18/santa-cruz-harbor-sees-more-than-6-million-in-tsunami-damage/.||https://twitter.com/VFisher45/status/1482419734112915457.

The tsunami caused at a minimum $3 million in damage to the Moss Landing Harbor District. Damage was inflicted on pilings, docks, the harbor channel and infrastructure. There is also potential damage to the shoreline and a possible need for dredging.||https://kion546.com/news/2022/03/04/funding-approved-for-damage-repairs-in-moss-landing-harbor-district-caused-by-tonga-tsunami/.

Four consecutive mornings of below-freezing temperatures forced some Sonoma County wine grape growers to protect swelling buds following prior weeks of warm, dry weather. Strong winds quickly spread this fire to approximately 20 acres, before it was contained. No damage to structures or persons was reported, but three businesses in the area were briefly evacuated. https://eastcountytoday.net/contra-costa-county-firefighters-battling-vegetation-fire-along-willow-pass/.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Search and Rescue team were unable to locate the diver who was swept out to sea by a rip current. Point Sur Buoy (Station 46239) measured average seas between 8 and 9 feet that day. Nearby Cabrillo Point buoy (Station 46240) in Monterey Bay, measured average seas 3 to 4 feet. Winds were not measured by the buoys, but the official forecast for the coastal zone from Point Pinos to Point Piedras Blancas called for NW winds 10-20 kt, with gusts up to 30 kt.

Two deaths were reported by police. Bodies were found in a parked car in a residential neighborhood in South San Francisco just before 6 p.m. Friday. It appears they were burning charcoal or a similar substance for heat ��� which likely filled the car with carbon monoxide, poisoning them. Temperatures dropped into the upper 30s F to low 40s F earlier that morning. The ground was wet from rain that had fallen the previous day.
Record daily low temperature, 36 deg F, reached in downtown Oakland (museum). The previous record was 38 deg F set in 1973.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Six unhoused residents died from cold-related illness between the 13th and 14th. Four of those were in San Jose aged 40s-70s, with two others in unspecified areas in Santa Clara county.
The Capitola Wharf at the Capitola State Beach broke in half, with a section of the wharf collapsing into the ocean.

A redwood tree fell onto a double wide mobile home on the 2800 block of Joy Road in Occidental, killing a 2-year old boy when the tree pinned him down on the couch in the home's living room. Rescue crews were called around 5:15 PM, and performed CPR on the boy, but the boy died at the scene.
The underpass of California Highway 1 under US Highway 101 in Manzanita flooded.
Flooding was reported on all lanes of Eastbound Interstate 580 near the Lakeshore Avenue exit in Oakland.
A mud slide blocked the entire westbound lane of California Highway 92 west of Pilarcitos Creek Road near Half Moon Bay.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Large waves took down the back of a house in Carmel Highlands.
The right hand side, and part of the number 2 (right) lane of the connector between Southbound Interstate 880 and Northbound Interstate 280 in western San Jose, was flooded.
Caltrain commuter rail reported that a tree fell on the overhead wires at its station in Burlingame, affecting Caltrain service in the area. The tree was not removed until 3 PM.
The eastbound lanes of California Highway 152 in the Pacheco Pass were blocked due to a downed tree.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A small tug and barge became unmoored in Monterey Bay at the Monterey Wharf. The Coast Guard brought the boat back to its mooring.

Major flooding closed US Highway 101 in both directions in the city of Gilroy, with the closure from Mesa Road to California State Route 25. The closure lasted for around 6 hours before traffic could be reopened.
The ASOS weather station at the San Francisco International Airport reported a gust of 60 mph.
A roof was blown off an apartment building in South San Francisco.

Roadway flooding was reported along Mark West Creek near the communities of Forestville and Trenton. A 43-year old woman from Ukiah was recovered on the 10th after her car got stuck in floodwaters. She had called 911 to report that her car was taking on water on Trenton-Healdsburg Road. The call cut out, and Sonoma County Fire sent swift water rescue gear around 10:10 AM on the 9th. A helicopter from the Sonoma County Sheriff's office was also involved. The search was called off at sunset, and by the morning of the 10th, the vehicle was found sitting in 8 to 10 feet of floodwaters.
Lightning struck a home in Monterey, resulting in an electrical surge and the oven sparking and overheating. Several homes on the same block also experienced power surges.
A mudslide caused California Highway 25 to become completely impassable south of Lonoak.
Trained spotter reported 4.45 inches of rain from 5 PM on December 30 to 5 PM on December 31.
Five people were transported to hospitals after black ice caused a three-car collision on US Highway 101 near the community of Asti, south of Cloverdale.

San Francisco Downtown site hit 5.46��� in the 24 hours of December 31st. This makes it the second wettest day on record, just 0.08��� less than 1st place (11/5/1994) with 5.54���||This also was 46.8% of the monthly rainfall (11.66���).
Oakland site had its wettest day on record (since 1970) with 4.75���, beating out the previous record set back on 1/4/1982 by just 0.01���||This day was 36% of December���s rainfall at this site.

Redwood City with 4.47. ||12/31/2022 was the 3rd wettest in a record that goes back to 1906. The daily rainfall made up 42.8% of December 2022's rainfall.||The wettest day on record at Redwood City was back on 10/13/1962 with 4.88 inches.

CHP reported flash flooding of US Highway 101 at Oyster Point Road in South San Francisco at 5:58 AM. By 10:58 AM, the entire roadway had flooded and the highway was closed. The flooding caused traffic backups and diversions with Interstate 280 as the alternate. The northbound lanes were reopened around 8 PM and the southbound lanes around 9 PM.

A 120-foot tall cypress tree fell on a 72-year old resident of Santa Cruz within Lighthouse Field State Beach around 1:30 PM during a major rain event. Victim was pronounced dead at the scene despite attempts at medical care. At time of event, multiple reports of flooding, mudslides, and fallen trees were reported across the CWA, especially in low-lying and hilly areas.

The Old Mill Mobile Home Park in Soquel was evacuated, after several mobile homes flooded. KSBW television quoted a resident as saying that the river rushed in so fast that barely had time to leave the house. The resident compared it to ocean waves in their backyard. County officials also stated that they would later find debris in Soquel Creek that blocked the flow.
The Santa Rita Creek overflowed into the Bolsa Knolls neighborhood of Salinas, as reported by KSBW television.
Heavy rain and high levels on Aptos Creek led to street flooding in the Rio Del Mar neighborhood of Aptos, trapping several people in their homes.

The roof of a Big 5 Sporting Goods store in San Ramon caved in the early morning hours of the 27th after a main beam broke in the center of the store. Local officials from the San Ramon Valley Protection District stated that they believed heavy rain was a factor in the roof collapse. The collapse caused water and debris to flow into the Big 5; the Rite Aid pharmacy next door was also flooded. Nearby businesses in the shopping center were closed as a precaution.
A tree fell onto power lines near the intersection of Moraga and Rimrock Roads, causing Moraga Road to be closed from Sky Hy Drive (Yes, that spelling is correct.) and St Mary's Road in Lafayette.

California Highway 1 was closed from Big Sur to Ragged Point due to rockslides across the highway in multiple places. As of April 2023, portions of the highway are still closed for repairs with no estimated time to reopen.
An eucalyptus tree fell onto an apartment building on Lynde Street in Oakland, forcing the evacuation of five families. The building was later red tagged.

Two separate landslides, one on Tuesday the 17th at 8:30 AM, and another on Wednesday the 18th during the morning, resulted in the suspension of ACE commuter rail service until the 23rd. The first landslide forced the ACE trains to stop on the section of rail parallel to Niles Canyon Road, with the train brought back to Pleasanton and bus bridges bringing passengers to their final destination.

A GMC Sierra heading southbound in the number one lane then crashed into the tree, killing the solo driver. A BMW also heading southbound in the number one lane then hit the tree, injuring two people including the driver and killing a passenger. At 7:30 AM the road was reopened.

Northbound lanes were opened at 3 PM with one southbound lane opened north of Summit Road by 5 PM.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: At 7:47 PM on the 22nd, a person reported a 3-year old boy unaccompanied at Moss Landing State Beach. The Coast Guard states that the boy said his mother went swimming and his 7-year old brother was missing. Cal Fire retrieved the mother from near Moss Landing Harbor; on Thursday, Monterey County Sheriff's Office reported she was dead in the water. The Coast Guard, Monterey County Sheriff's Office, and North County Fire started to search for the 7-year old boy; the search was suspended at 2 AM Thursday and resumed Thursday morning. On Saturday, the Monterey County Sheriff's Department confirmed that the 7-year old boy was found dead in the water; a dive team found the missing child about 10 feet below the surface of the lagoon at 11:20 AM.
CHP reported a mud slide moving debris on California Highway 116.
CHP reported a large land slide blocking southbound lanes of US Highway 101 near the Waldo Grade.
Flooding reported on the ramp from Southbound California Highway 87 to Northbound Interstate 280, with 1 foot of water over the roadway.
Trained spotter around 1 mile south of Sausalito reported a gust of 65 mph.

events.event_narrative: A 21-year-old male residing in Pacific Grove drowned in the sea off Carmel-by-the-Sea on Thursday August 31, 2023. The man had planned to go fishing north of Stewarts Cove on August 30 and did not return home that night as planned. Family members found his car in the Carmel River beach parking lot and reported him missing around 11 AM. The body was reported to authorities around 11:45 AM and recovered just after noon off Scenic Road. A small craft advisory for northwest winds 15 to 25 knots was in effect Wednesday, August 30 including during the evening until 9 pm. Lighter northwest winds and no small craft advisory were in effect Thursday morning, August 31, when the deceased male was found. Buoy 46042 reported wave heights of 6 to 9 feet on August 30, with periods of 7 to 9 seconds and wind gusts up to 25 knots. Wave heights at buoy 46239 ranged between 7 to 8.5 feet at 8 to 12 seconds, generally from the west or northwest. At Cabrillo Point, wave heights ranged from 3 to 3.5 feet at 8 to 12 seconds.

The girl was recovered and taken to the hospital, where she was pronounced dead. The man remains missing, and the search was called off the next day.

A landslide along California Highway 1 near the Rocky Creek Bridge on March 30 forced the closure of the road at Palo Colorado. The landslide took out parts of the southbound lane of Highway 1 with the northbound lane also in danger. Combined with earlier closures of Highway 1 at Limekiln State Park near Lucia and the Nacimiento-Ferguson Road due to the Dolan Fire, the closure left the area around Big Sur isolated from the outside world. As of March 31, vehicles are only allowed to travel to the north in corridors at 8 AM and 4 PM daily.||The event followed a very active 48 hours of weather with heavy rain, strong winds and a rare severe thunderstorm warning. MRMS rainfall rates were as high as 1.9/hour on the 29th and a nearby gauge recorded 3.9 in 48 hours. Winds were also strong, with radar velocity data suggesting up to 60 mph gusts and nearby observations as high as 48 mph. A gale warning was issued for the coastal zone at 235AM on Thursday, March 28th. Valid 9AM-9PM Friday, easily verified by radar data, but no in situ observations are available. A wind advisory was issued at 205AM Thursday, March 28th and upgraded to a high wind warning at 215AM on Friday, March 29th. The high wind warning was valid 1AM-9PM Friday, and verified by a 62 mph gusts recorded at Lime Creek Road (741 ft). 5 separate Special Marine Warnings were issued for the affected coastline on Friday for winds greater than 40 kts and possible waterspouts. The issue times were 1226PM, 143PM, 243PM, 430PM, and 457PM. Again, these were only verified with radar data due to limited in-situ measurements over the water. A Severe Thunderstorm Warning was issued at 312PM Friday for 60 mph wind gusts and a possible tornado based on radar indicated rotation. There were no reports of a tornado, and the highest observed wind gusts at the time of the warning were 46 mph, although a 62 mph gust was recorded at 540PM, after the warning expired (see high wind warning above). A Flood Advisory was issued at 448PM Friday that covered the slide area for urban and small stream flooding. While most of the severe weather in this area occurred on Friday, there were 2 Special Weather Statements issued at 221AM and 402AM for 30-40 mph wind and pea sized hail just south of the slide. The first was verified with a 31mph gust at 250AM from Pfeiffer Ridge Road.

events.event_narrative: A 55-year old man was last seen with a surfboard around 10AM at Drakes Beach off of Point Reyes National Seashore. His surfboard was found washed ashore at Drakes Beach at approximately 1:00PM with 9-1-1 first called at approximately 2:36PM. First responders shortly began the search and a Search and Rescue Team was dispatched. A search and rescue spot forecast was requested at 5:15PM and completed at approximately 5:28PM. Search and Rescue teams located the body at 5:33PM in the ocean approximately 2.5 miles northwest of the Drakes Beach Parking Area. The surfer was pronounced deceased at 5:35PM and identified. Local buoy data from Buoy 46013 reported sustained winds between 20-25 knots and gusts between 30-40 knots between 9AM to 5PM on 1 May. Wave heights were reported to be between 9 to 10 feet.

A 32-foot long pleasure boat capsized near the Golden Gate Bridge on April 14. Coast Guard watchstanders received a notification at around 9:30 AM from a pilot boat captain that four boaters were in need of rescue after the boat capsized. A San Francisco Police Department boat crew and a pilot boat arrived to rescue the crew, and transferred them to a Coast Guard motor lifeboat, which brought them to Horseshoe Bay to be treated for hypothermia. At the time of the initial notification, the San Francisco Bar buoy (46237) reported significant waves of 1.8 m (around 6 feet) from 287 degrees, a dominant period of 12 seconds, and an average period of 8.1 seconds. Swell waves were 1.4 m (around 4.5 ft) at 11.8 seconds from the west-northwest, wind waves were 1.1 m (around 3.5 ft) at 9.5 seconds from the west-northwest.

Several people were overcome by the heat at the American Canyon High School graduation. Three people were taken to the hospital and two more got medical attention on site. Temperatures in the area reached 91 degrees.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: San Jose police responded to a call around 8 PM to a homeless man who was found dead. The day saw San Jose tie an all-time daily record with a high of 102.

A 28-year old man drowned in the Russian River near the Patterson Point Preserve on Wednesday July 3, while seeking relief from the heat. Observers reported that the man was sucked down by a whirlpool around 6 PM and never came back on shore; his body was found near Monte Rio on Friday after a search.

A 51-year old man drowned in the Russian River on Saturday July 6. A group of paddleboarders noticed a commotion near the Bohemian Highway Bridge around 6:40 PM and noticed the man in distress. They attempted CPR until fire officials arrived and attempted life saving measures for 25 minutes until he was pronounced dead.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Through the month of July, 28 deaths across Santa Clara County were being investigated for heat-related impacts. 19 of those were reported from July 1 to July 11; the remaining 9 died on unknown days. Ages ranged from 32 to 84. Of the 19 people who died from the 1st to the 11th, four were homeless, one was in a transitional housing program, and nine were over 65.

A sneaker wave killed a couple from San Jose who were standing along West Cliff Drive in Santa Cruz. The couple stood on a rock to take pictures when the wave hit the rock. A rescue swimmer pulled the victims onto a boat, but was unable to revive the couple.

The Point Fire started near Stewarts Point Skaggs Springs Road in the Dry Creek valley north of Healdsburg, and was first detected at 12:33 PM on June 16. The fire destroyed ten structures, including three homes, and damaged another two homes. The fire was contained on June 24th.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Eight heat-related deaths were recorded in Santa Clara County from July 7 to 12.
Sonoma County reported 19 calls to 911 for heat related illnesses between October 2 and 7.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: The Coast Guard received a report about six people on an overdue boat near Bodega Bay at 11:40 PM Saturday from the Sonoma County Sheriff's Office. The boaters departed Westside Marina on a 21-foot long blue and white vessel at 3 PM and were expected back by 7 PM. A 13-year old boy was found alive off South Salmon Creek Beach at 8 AM on Sunday, with an older boy found dead around 10:15 AM. The search was suspended around 6:30 PM pending new information.||Wind gusts at the Bodega Bay buoy (46013) reached around 27 knots during the afternoon and evening of Saturday the 2nd. Significant wave heights were 8 to 9.5 feet from the west-northwest.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A hiker called 911 at 7 AM on Monday and reported that they had seen a boat capsize off Mussel Point and Bodega Head with two people onboard. The boat was 20 feet long and manufactured by Boston Whaler. A man was found dead on Bodega Dunes Beach at 7:40 AM. His companion remains missing. ||A Small Craft Advisory was in effect for the waters off Bodega bay at the time of the advisory. Mean wave direction was WNW with heights ranging between 8 and 12 feet at the Bodega Bay Buoy (Station 46013) during the pre-dawn hours on Monday (11/4). NNW to NW winds ranged between 13 and 19 knots with peak gusts around 25 knots during the pre-dawn hours on Monday (11/4).

A 911 caller reported to Sonoma County dispatch that they had seen a car go into floodwaters near Mays Canyon Road and Highway 116. Rescue crews arrived and found the vehicle, and the driver was found dead.
One person was injured when a tree fell on their home on Cozey Court in Forestville. The Sonoma County Fire District responded to the home after the report at 4:30 PM.
Social media user on X (formerly Twitter) reported flooding at their home in Fulton.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Sonoma County 911 dispatch was called on November 18 around 1:45pm PST after a caller reported seeing three people aboard a boat being battered by waves and waving a red flag for help. Four boaters were eventually rescued and taken to the hospital, an additional boater washed up dead on the shore.

A tornado warning for San Francisco and San Mateo Counties was issued at 5:51 AM after a rotating thunderstorm was observed off the coast of San Francisco. This is the first tornado warning issued on record for the city of San Francisco, using records that extend to at least 2005 and potentially since 1986. After an NWS storm survey that extended from the west side of Golden Gate Park to the Richmond district, it was determined that damage along the path of the cell was consistent with straight line wind gusts around 80 mph.

A Special Weather Statement was issued at 1:07 PM, followed by a Severe Thunderstorm Warning at 1:25 PM, for a strong thunderstorm that impacted western Santa Cruz County. Following the impact, social media videos and reports indicated that a tornado briefly touched down in the Scotts Valley region. A team from the National Weather Service San Francisco Bay Area conducted a storm survey in Scotts Valley. The team identified a swath of tornadic damage that began near the intersection of Mount Hermon Rd and Lockewood Ln and continued southeast along Mount Hermon Rd until just short of Kings Village Rd. A wide range of damage was observed including: downed trees, downed power poles, trees stripped of branches, numerous overturned vehicles, and damaged street signs.  Based on these damage indicators the survey team assessed a maximum wind speed of 90 mph, which is a weak EF1 tornado. Five people, including a firefighter, were injured by the tornado, and six cars were turned over including a pickup truck from Cal Fire.

While there are few observations from the San Pablo Bay itself, nearby weather stations recorded a maximum gust of around 40-50 mph on the 14th.

Around 150 feet of the Santa Cruz wharf collapsed and fell into Monterey Bay. Three workers from the city of Santa Cruz were dropped into the water. Lifeguards rescued two of the workers, while the third was able to swim to shore.

events.event_narrative: Marina Police received a call around noon about a man in his 30s swept into the sea at the Marina State Beach at noon on December 23. Bystanders tried to assist the man but the waves were too strong. Marina Police suspended their search after two hours as wave conditions became hazardous. On December 29, a body was found floating in Monterey Bay around 4 miles off Marina State Beach. The Monterey County Sheriff's Office called the Coast Guard for assistance, but they were unable to retrieve the body.

A witness said that the man was knocked into the water while standing on a rock. The search turned into a rescue mission after 45 minutes, and searches continued into Tuesday.

An elderly man went missing while walking his dog in Garland Ranch Regional Park, and was last heard from around 10:30 AM. Around 11 AM, hikers found his dog and returned it to the man's family, who reported him missing at noon. Monterey County park rangers were assisted by local and state resources in a swift-water search, who ultimately found the man's body in Carmel River.

A water rescue operation occurred in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Davenport on April 7. First responders were called to Davenport Landing at 2:17 PM as four people were in the water and struggling to return to shore. Three rescue swimmers from Cal Fire and two from California State Parks jumped in and brought all four people to shore unharmed.

The Midway Fire was first noted at 2:51 PM in eastern Alameda County, at Midway Road and Patterson Pass Road near the city of Tracy. The fire caused a closure of Interstate 580, a key highway connecting the Bay Area to the Central Valley, for approximately 2 and a half hours from around 3:45 PM to around 6:25 PM, with lanes remaining closed through around 8:40 PM. The fire was mapped at 262 acres, and had burned past Interstate 580 and the Alameda-San Joaquin county line up to the California Aqueduct near Tracy.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A twin-engine Beechcraft, tail number N8796R, departed from San Carlos Airport in the Bay Area at approximately 10:07 p.m., heading to Monterey Regional Airport. However, around 10:38 p.m., the aircraft crashed into the ocean 200-300 yards off Point Pinos near Sunset Drive and Jewell Avenue. At the time of the incident, Monterey Regional Airport reported IFR conditions with ceilings at 800 feet. Rescuers found one of the victims dead in the water, with aircraft debris washing up ashore.

The Pickett Fire broke out to the north of Calistoga on August 21 around 3 PM, and would eventually burn 6803 acres, leading to evacuations across mainly rural areas of Napa County, including the community of Aetna Springs. Hot and dry conditions, with warm overnight lows and poor overnight humidity recoveries in the higher elevations, presented elevated fire weather threats across the interior through the first few days of the fire's lifecycle.

A strong thunderstorm cell touched down just south of Ano Nuevo State Park at 4:23 PM. Video from a farm near the location showed damage to structures, sparking speculation of a possible tornado. Subsequently, an NWS team conducted a storm survey at the site. The team identified damage consistent with straight line winds. Damage was noted from the coast, just south of A��o Nuevo State Park, eastward about 3/4 of a mile. This damage included, but not limited to, a hoop house visqueen cover being torn off, structural damage to two hoop houses, a large water storage tank being transported over a 1/4 mile, and moderately large diameter coastal cypress trees being snapped. There was one item seen transported counter to straight line wind flow and these were determined to have been caught up in very small scale temporary terrain driven  rotation. There is no indication in the damage field of tornadic activity. While the radar signature did show rotation at elevation while approaching the coast, it appears to collapse as it comes  ashore, lending itself to thunderstorm outflow and a straight line wind event.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Two people died after a family of four was swept out to sea at Garrapata Beach on November 14th by a wave estimated at 15 to 20 feet high. An off-duty state park lifeguard noticed the family in distress around 12:50 PM, and pulled a father and mother towards shore. A seven-year old girl, the daughter of the couple, was swept away. The father received CPR and was sent to the hospital where he was pronounced dead. The mother was also transported to a hospital and had signs of hypothermia. The search for the 7-year girl continued into the following weekend, and she was eventually found 100 yards offshore at around 1:25 PM on Sunday. At the time of the incident, an offshore buoy (46239) reported a water temperature of 59 degrees and waves of 13.7 feet from the west-northwest at a dominant period of 14 seconds.

Shortly after 9AM on November 5, 2025, rescue crews were deployed to The Hook near Capitola as two surfers were reported in distress. One surfer was able to make it past the line of breaking waves, while the other was caught in them. When the surfer was pulled from the water, they were unconscious and was rushed to the hospital. The surfer was pronounced dead at a hospital two days later.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A 35-year old man and two women were hit by a large wave on November 22. The two women were able to self-rescue, but the man was not. Just after 3 PM, the Monterey County Sheriff's Office and California State Parks launched a rescue effort for the man. Around 4:24 PM, a U.S. Coast Guard helicopter located what appeared to be a body in the water; however, due to dangerous surf conditions, visual contact was lost and the individual could not be relocated. Formal search operations were ended on November 26.

A 32-year old man died after drowning off Bean Hollow State Beach in southern San Mateo County. California State Parks was informed of a possible drowning around 3:25 PM on December 3, when a woman told them that she and her husband were fishing on the rocks, when the woman went to her car and returned to find her husband gone. A bystander saw a body in the water, and Cal Fire retrieved the body and attempted lifesaving measures, which ultimately failed. The man was pronounced dead at the scene.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: An 87-year old male died from hypothermia near the Alum Rock neighborhood of San Jose on the morning of December 20, with hypertensive cardiovascular disease as a contributing factor. The low temperature at San Jose International Airport that day was 60, but this is likely to be warmer than the temperature in areas of San Jose away from the downtown core.

The Coast Guard Sector San Francisco reported that watch standers received a report around 6:30 PM on February 6 for two surfers in the water calling for help around 600 feet from the Santa Cruz Lighthouse. Coast Guard air and marine resources, Santa Cruz Fire Department and Dispatch, and Civil Air Patrol assisted in the search. The search continued until the search was suspended around 8 AM February 7. No reports of missing surfers were received by local authorities or through social media outreach, it is presumed that the two surfers were able to self-rescue. At the time of the initial report, buoy 46236 reported swell waves of 11 feet at 14.6 seconds from the west, with wind waves of 4 ft at 9.9 seconds.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: The California Highway Patrol received initial reports of a vehicle going over the cliff off of Highway One into the ocean at 4:20 PM on 2/10/2026. Nearby PGE observation stations reported 40 mph (Coast Road, 404 ft in elevation, north of accident site) and 45 mph (Funt Ranch, 995 ft in elevation, due east and uphill of accident site) gusts at 4:00PM. Sites in the wider vicinity of the accident reported light rain was occurring between 4PM and 5PM. The CHP incident report stated at 4:20PM that it was too windy to see vehicle at the bottom of the cliff. The CHP report mentions a 30 mph gust at 4:52 PM after Coast Guard operations began to reach the vehicle. The Monterey County Sheriff stated that weather conditions made recovery efforts extremely challenging. The victim was recovered around 8:45 PM, one fatality was confirmed as a result of the accident. At the time of the incident, a Wind Advisory was in effect for the Big Sur coast due to the strong wind gusts in the area.

A small sedan attempted to ford Tres Pinos Creek along Browns Valley Road near Paicines on the night of February 17, with first responders responding to the scene during the night. The next morning, the driver was found walking along Highway 25 asking about the location of the passenger. The passenger's body was eventually found a mile downstream of where the car had gotten stranded. The driver was later arrested on charges of gross vehicular manslaughter. At the time of the incident, the TESC1 river gauge on Tres Pinos Creek measured stages above 2 feet, compared to a typical stage of less than a foot.

A boat carrying six people, two adults and their four children, capsized off Steamer Lane near Santa Cruz around 11:45 AM on February 6. The children were wearing life vests, but the parents were not. Around ten surfers, one of whom was 14, helped to rescue the family and bring them to safety; patrol boats and ambulances arrived within minutes. The people were taken to a hospital and recovered. At the time of the incident, buoy 46236 reported swell waves of 8 ft at 16.7 seconds from the west, with wind waves of 4 ft at 9.9 seconds.

Additional rockslides were reported on the highway between Lucia and the Monterey-SLO county line. The cumulative impact of all the rockslides forced the closure of Highway 1 from Pardington Lane to Ragged Point at 11 PM on February 10, reopening at 8:45 AM the next day.

events.event_narrative: On April 1, California Fish and Wildlife received a report of an adult male kayaker reported troubled by weather near the break wall of the Monterey Harbor. The report was relayed to the Coast Guard by 12:32 PM, and Coast Guard Station Monterey launched, arrived on the scene, and recovered the kayaker and the kayak. The kayaker was taken to the Monterey Harbor boat launch, with no medical attention required. At the time of the incident, Scripps coastal station 46240 at Cabrillo Point reported a north swell of one foot at 14.3 seconds, and a north-northwest wind wave of 1 foot at 9.1 seconds. Buoy 46236 in the Monterey Canyon area reported a west swell of 1.5 feet at 13.3 seconds, and a west-northwest wind wave of 2 feet at 9.1 seconds.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A 37-year old woman from Los Angeles died after her kayak overturned on March 21 in Tomales Bay near Mendoza Beach. First responders received reports of the overturned kayak around 6 PM and multiple rescue crews from the Marin and Sonoma County Sheriff's Offices, Marin County Fire, the U.S. Coast Guard and the National Park Service responded. The woman was found unresponsive in the water, and was hoisted out of the bay and taken to shore for lifesaving measures. She was then taken to the hospital, where she was declared dead. The woman's boyfriend and a dog were located near the kayak; both survived although the boyfriend was treated for hypothermia. A nearby weather station showed winds were from the NWW that afternoon around 20-24 mph with gusts from 25-34 mph.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: A 41-year old man died on the western side of San Jose early on the morning of March 18. The Santa Clara County Medical Examiner-Coroner's office reported that while the immediate cause was hypertensive cardiovascular disease, environmental heat exposure was a significant factor.

Strong winds caused a 130 foot fir tree to fall onto a home just north of Ben Lomond, CA. The tree also snapped a power pole and downed wires as it fell across State Highway Nine. Highway Nine was closed for the remainder of the day as workers removed the tree.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Heavy rain over the fire scarred Santa Lucia Mountains resulted in a few debris flows and flash flooding along the Big Sur Coast.  The Juan Higuera Creek, Redwood Creek and Big Sur River filled with debris flooding the Grange in Big Sur and producing a debris flow through a residence.  Also, a foot bridge and two fish ponds were destroyed as a six foot debris flow passed by yet another residence. Highway One was closed along the Big Sur Coast as rocks and trees settled on the roadway.
Strong wind accompanied by heavy rain brought trees down across the San Francisco North Bay area closing roadways. A tree fell across Calistoga Road at Petrified Forest Road closing the highway.

Strong wind accompanied by heavy rain brought trees down across the San Francisco North Bay area closing roadways. A tree fell across Lytton Springs Road near Dry Creek Road closing the eastbound lane. Also, about 250 customers in Occidental lost power on Saturday associated with downed power lines due to trees falling on elevated wires.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind accompanied by heavy rain caused about 390 customers in Fort Ross to lose power.

Heavy rain caused many vehicle collisions in the San Francisco East Bay area on Saturday. One crash in particular resulted in a vehicle carrying six passengers flipping into the canal that splits Hegenberger Expressway near Hamilton Street in Oakland. The nineteen year old male driver died in the crash (indirect fatality).
A wet mountain road caused a man to veer off highway 152 near Watsonville resulting in his death.
Heavy rain caused a fatality of a 32 year-old man when his vehicle collided with another vehicle. Highways 116 and 121 were closed for about three hours after the collision.

Several trees were blown down at the Hayward Japanese Gardens as strong wind gusts develop Tuesday night. The Gardens' centerpiece, a seventy-one foot tall Italian Stone Pine, and eight other trees were uprooted closing the park for several days.

Freezing temperatures combined with moisture from rain and snow to cause several minor accidents on mountain highways. Authorities closed mountain roads for several hours as sand was placed on roadways. Primary routes such as Calistoga and Porter Creek Roads were closed along with alternate routes due to the icy conditions.

Freezing temperatures combined with residual moisture from the previous days' rain to cause several minor traffic accidents. Icy conditions led to at least three collisions on Highway 4, Highway 24, and on San Pablo Dam Road. Also, black ice is suspected as the culprit in two other accidents, one in Martinez and the other in Pleasanton.

Strong winds associated with this fast moving storm kept local fire fighters busy responding to 23 reports of downed trees from Daly City to Redwood City. Another accident possibly resulting from inclement weather conditions involved at least two vehicles, one an SUV which flipped onto its roof, along Highway 101 closing one lane and an on ramp at Sister Cities Boulevard in South San Francisco.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Strong and gusty winds shattered a power pole in San Jose leaving around 900 homes without power for several hours.

Strong southerly winds resulted in power outages for hundreds in Pacifica, Half Moon Bay, San Bruno and Burlingame. Along with the loss of power local fire fighters responded to numerous reports of down trees. During the period in which the weather was most severe a car drove off of Highway 1 near Verdi road just south of Half Moon Bay. The occupants suffered only minor injuries.
Strong wind reaching speeds of 48 mph sent a tree crashing into a house in Oakland causing minor damage. Also, about 2500 customers lost power in downtown Oakland.
Strong winds mixed with saturated soils and caused several trees to fall and block Highway 9 near Pierce Road, west of Saratoga.
A trained spotter reported one foot of snow had fallen overnight at Mount Bocci, near Mount Umunhum, at an elevation above 2500 feet.

Strong wind sent numerous tree limbs into power lines resulting in power outages in Santa Cruz County. The strong wind combined with saturated soils from heavy rain to uproot trees causing road closures and additional power outages as trees knocked power lines to the ground.

Strong wind and heavy rain caused a tree to be uprooted by Mt. Carmel Baptist Church in Oakland. Also of note, at 5:45 p.m. the City of San Mateo reported a 12,000 gallon sewage release which overflowed into the storm drains due to rain water surcharge from the storm overwhelming the system.

High wind knocked down numerous trees in the Santa Cruz Mountains causing Highway 9 at Highway 236 to close at 6:30 a.m. and knocked down power lines closing Thurber Lane at Twelfth Avenue during the morning. Trees and branches slowed traffic along Highway 17, Bear Creek Road and Middle Ellen Road.

A fatal accident occurred just after 4:00 p.m. on northbound Highway 1 near Rio Del Mar Boulevard when a car spun out on the wet highway, went over an embankment and struck a tree. The 29-year-old male driver sustained minor injuries while the 27-year-old female passenger was fatality injured.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A 40-foot pine tree was uprooted on the third fairway of the Pebble Beach Golf Course due to gusty winds of up to an estimated 60 mph. At 2:40 p.m. the Point Sur Lighthouse observation station reported a peak wind gust to 58 mph.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind coupled with heavy rain along the San Francisco Area's North Bay coast knocked down power lines, snapped small tree limbs, downed trees and caused minor rock slides. About 600 customers in and around Jenner lost power from 3 a.m. until around 1 p.m.  Point Reyes Lighthouse observation station reported a peak wind gust to 66 mph at 12:40 a.m.
The Pigeon Point observation station reported a peak wind gust to 58 mph at 3:09 a.m.

Strong winds caused a power outage in and around Sonoma. About 350 customers lost power at 8:15 a.m.

Strong wind caused the closure of State Route 92, just east of Skylawn Cemetery, in the Redwood City Area, due to a fallen tree blocking the roadway. The roadway reopened at approximately 3:54 a.m. Also of note, minor flooding was reported at the westbound Jackson Street offramp from Interstate 880 in Oakland, and at the tunnel at Yerba Buena Island on the westbound lanes of the Bay Bridge.

At approximately 2:18 a.m. strong wind knocked a tree onto State Route 92 causing its closer at the Junction of State Route 35 in Half Moon Bay. The roadway was reopened at approximately 3:56 a.m. In Palo Alto strong wind downed a 60 foot live coastal oak tree. Along with damage to a car and a house on Emerson Street, the tree took out a power pole.
At approximately 4:37 a.m. US 101 was closed to northbound traffic at Lucky Drive in Corte Madera due to flooding. At approximately 6:32 a.m. the roadway was reopened.
Strong winds caused power outages across the San Francisco Bay Area including a 1000 customer outage in Orinda.

events.event_narrative: A 36-foot boat capsized in rough seas resulting in two people rescued and the drowning of a male fisherman. Wave heights at nearby buoys were reported at three to three and a half meters.
A large bay tree snapped in half and fell across power lines in Monte Rio and resulted in closing Starrett Hill Drive near Moscow Road.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds caused an estimated 100 foot tall, five foot diameter based pine tree to fall onto power lines at the junction of Shoreline Highway and Panoramic Highway around 11:10 a.m. PDT. The intersection was closed for five hours as crews removed the debris. The seven customers who lost power had it restored by 6:30 p.m. PDT.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / HOLLISTER VALLEY / CARMEL VALLEY
events.event_narrative: Strong winds toppled a pine tree at the Saddle Ranch Resort onto a trailer trapping the occupant inside for an hour before he was extricated uninjured. Also, in and around Carmel Valley, there were many roads temporarily blocked due to trees and limbs blown down by the wind.
Strong winds caused a large pine tree to come crashing down onto Green Valley Road in front of Pinto Lake City Park.

Heavy rain fell on top of a recently burned forest causing flash flooding and debris flows. More than three feet of mud covered State Route One closing it for several hours. Vehicles parked at the Big Sur Lodge were stuck in mud and debris. One vehicle was even forced into a culvert and buried. At least three separate debris flows were reported along Highway One, all within a 3 mile span.
An eighteen inch thick tree came down on a home just off the village square in Nicasio, destroying part of the front porch.

A tree fell into a power line on Pine Street in Novato causing a small fire and knocking out power along the street. In Healdsburg, strong wind brought trees down into power lines knocking out power to downtown for about an hour. Downed trees also caused damage, started small fires and produced power outages in Santa Rosa. Over 5,000 customers lost power during this storm and a recently restored home on Belmont Court was damaged as a large Douglas Fir tree crashed onto it. On Hearn Avenue and on Montgomery Drive two cars were damaged as trees fell onto them.
Strong wind blew a two feet thick, 25 feet tall tree down into a yard on Rockaway Street in San Francisco.

High winds wreak havoc along the San Francisco Bay Area shoreline causing numerous power outages, downed trees and forcing a big-rig onto its side. At 5:35 p.m. PST a big-rig blew over in the west bound lane of the San Mateo Bridge closing the entire bridge for more than an hour. Shortly afterwards a seventy foot fishing vessel was blown into the bridge after losing power. At 4:54 p.m. PST the Redwood City Mesonet observation site reported a gust to 50 knots.

Wind blown trees fell onto roadways and into a home in La Honda. Alpine Road was closed for about eight hours as trees were removed while Redwood Drive was closed for almost 24 hours after a large Douglas Fir tree fell over and into a home. On Highway 84 near the intersection of Redwood Terrace a downed power line sparked a small grass fire.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Downed trees crushed cars in San Jose and clogged major intersections including Monterey and Brokaw Roads, and Meridian Avenue and Branham Lane. Power outages also occurred as trees brought power lines to the ground with 4,600 customers losing power.

Power lines were ripped to the ground as trees were blown onto them. Both the 400 block of Summer Avenue in Rio del Mar and along Paul Minnie Avenue in Live Oak experienced downed power lines. In all, nearly 6,000 customers in Santa Cruz County were without power at the height of this storm.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / HOLLISTER VALLEY / CARMEL VALLEY
events.event_narrative: Strong winds toppled a large eucalyptus tree onto a vehicle and across Highway 68 near the Toro Cafe. The tree sheared power lines on its way down causing a power outage. Other power lines were blown down around Monterey County affecting 4,500 customers.

Two men were in the surf about waist deep near stairway 24, just south of the Cliff House on Ocean Beach, San Francisco when a large wave knocked then off their feet and swept them away. The two men were caught in a rip current and only one of them survived.
An overloaded electric transformer failed in Oakland causing more than 5,000 customers to lose power for about three hours.

Several people sought medical attention due to heat-induced fainting spells in Anitoch and Walnut Creek. Also, an electric transformer failed sparking a fire in Walnut Creek near the intersection of Wiget Lane and Ygnacio Valley Road causing 108 customers to lose power. The fire damaged nearby vegetation and an olive tree.
Temperatures rose into the 80s across San Francisco.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures rose into the 80s along the coast of the Northern San Francisco Bay Area.
Temperatures rose into the mid to upper 90s in the interior valleys of the Northern San Francisco Bay Area.
Temperatures rose into the 80sto lower 90s in the mountains of the Northern San Francisco Bay Area.
Temperatures rose into the upper 80s to mid 90s across the peninsula of the San Francisco Bay Area.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures rose into the upper 80s to mid 90s across the mountains of the East San Francisco Bay Area. One hiker was escorted off of Mount Diablo by fire fighter due to heat exhaustion.
Temperatures rose into the 80s to lower 90s across the mountains of Santa Cruz County.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures rose into the 90s to just over 100 degrees in the valleys of Santa Clara County. Cooling centers were open across the area to mitigate heat related illnesses.
Dense fog along with a slippery road surface caused eight traffic collisions along highway 17 in the Santa Cruz county mountains. No major injures were reported.

Heavy rain caused many trees throughout Sonoma County to fall resulting in closed roads, damaged homes, injuries and even a death of a five-year-old boy. An oak tree fell onto an occupied car on Bennett Valley Road killing the child and injuring his father. Another oak tree crashed down on a house in Boyes Hot Springs along Poplar Avenue. And, yet another oak tree fell across Highway 12 in Schellville closing the highway to traffic between Watmaugh and Highway 121 for almost three hours.

A father and son were hiking during the hottest time of the day when the father collapse due to heat exhaustion and dehydration. The father died on the trail and the boy was taken to a hospital where he recovered.

About 47,000 residents lost power around San Francisco as thunderstorms rolled through the city/county.  The largest outage affected 36,000 customers in parts of Sunset, Glen Park and Park Merced neighborhoods.  One lightning strike hit a power transformer causing it to explode.  Besides the total destruction of the power transformer, two vehicles were damaged at the intersection of Broderick and Sacramento Roads.

Lightning struck a house and surrounding trees in the 300 block of Summit Avenue damaging two 200-foot-tall Redwood trees and a driveway.  Also the lightning fried the television and a video game system.
Roughly 270 customers lost power in Pescadero as strong and gusty winds blew tree limbs onto power lines.
Roughly 23 customers lost power in East Palo Alto and Woodside as strong and gusty winds blew tree limbs onto power lines.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Damaging winds combined with rain soaked soils to knock down dozens of trees and broke numerous tree limbs.  Power outages were rampant.

A very large oak tree fell onto a house and high-tension communication lines in Healdsburg knocking down the home's chimney, separating it from the roof.  In Novato, a large tree fell across Alameda del Prado causing lane restrictions.  And, on the Richmond-San Rafael Bridge, strong winds toppled a big rig onto another vehicle. Elsewhere in the North Bay Interior Valleys dozens of downed trees caused roadways to close and the occurrence of thousands of power outages.

Heavy rain and overwhelmed storm drains led to a couple of flooded businesses in San Anselmo along Greenfield Avenue. Over 6 inches of rain fell within a 12 hour period.  Kentfield shattered the 24 hour rainfall record for October 13 reporting 6.14 inches. Also, the morning commute was bogged down due to flooding along Highway 101 near Lucky Drive and Tamalpais Drive in Corte Madera, and at the junction of Highway 1 in Marin City.

The westbound lane of Imola Avenue at Lernhart Street near South Jefferson Street was closed due to flooding.  Heavy rain along with overwhelmed storm drains caused the flooding.  Also, minor rock and mud slides occurred across Butts Canyon Road just before the Lake County line.

Flooding brought road closures and partial road closures to Scenic Avenue at Old River Road in Forestville, Clayton Road in Franz Valley, Stewarts Point at Skaggs Springs Road, Kruse Road near Seaview, Pine Flat Road, along the Bohemian Highway near Freestone, River Road at Mirabel and Coleman Valley Road near Occidental.  Highway 101 dropped to one lane in sections between Windsor and Santa Rosa after culverts and drainage measures were overwhelmed with runoff from heavy rain.  The heavy rain also caused damage to vineyards as rot began to spread to the merlot and syrah grapes.

Strong winds across San Francisco brought numerous trees down and caused thousands of buildings to lose power. On Hyde Street near Green Street a parked car was crushed as a three-story high eucalyptus tree fell onto it while a truck just pulling away received a cracked windshield. At the San Francisco State University campus a few trees were uprooted near Mary Park and Mary Ward halls. Elsewhere in the city a tree fell across the entire span of Broadway between Powell and Stockton Streets.  Over 125 calls to the Department of Public Works regarding tree issues occurred.

Shortly before 6:00 a.m., the California Highway Patrol closed the Interstate 280 extension between Sixth Street and Highway 101 because of flooding.  At 7:00 a.m. all lanes of Southbound Interstate 280 at Cesar Chavez Street were flooded.
Trees were blown down onto Fort Ross Road at Bohan Dillon Road near Seaview blocking all lanes.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: High winds were reported throughout San Francisco's east bay hills and the Diablo Mountain Range.  Here are other measured peak wind gust reports from RAWSs:  Las Trampas - 60 mph at 12:30 p.m., Calaveras Road - 66 mph at 3:30 p.m., Rose Peak - 59 mph at 9:28 a.m., and Oakland North - 58 mph.

Pleasanton was hit hard by the high winds with numerous trees down. At least two vehicles were damaged as trees fell onto them.  Also, there were 30 phone calls to the city's dispatch center with tree or tree limb related problems.

High winds were reported throughout San Francisco Bay shoreline.  Here are other measured peak wind gust reports from automated systems:  Point San Pablo Bay Area Air Quality Management District - 74 mph and San Francisco Airport - 62 mph.  The high winds knocked down power lines and trees causing hundreds of thousands of people to lose power. A huge oak tree crushed a house in Redwood City and brought down power lines. Also in Redwood City, dozens of trees were toppled, including at least two that hit houses or parked cars. Within San Mateo County at least 47 trees and 31 sets of power lines were knocked over.  In Los Altos, three power lines and 18 trees were knocked down.  Several of those trees fell on homes causing structural damage.  In Milpitas, a large tree landed on a house on the 1300 block of Lassen Avenue causing minor damage.
Very bad flooding occurred on Interstate 580 near the intersection of Harrison Street due to heavy rain.
Flooding occurred along Interstate 880 near the intersection of Interstate 980.
Standing water covered the entire Benedict Drive onramp to Interstate 580.

The Marina Street apartments in Antioch were evacuated due to flooding of surrounding streets.  Firefighters had to help two adults and a baby from the apartment building, which was surrounded by waist deep water.
Heavy rain caused major flooding on Bernal Avenue at Valley Avenue.

Damage was done to an underground utility trench along Crest Road in Piedmont from torrential rains. Rain water found its way through cracks in the sidewalk and percolated up through the street. As a result, two and a half feet of sand covering a conduit was disturbed or washed away leaving damaged sidewalks.

The Spring Valley RAWS reported a gust to 62 mph at 11:19 p.m. PDT.  In Pescadero, a large tree was blown onto North Street at Pescadero Road blocking both lanes of traffic.  Wind also caused power outages all across San Mateo County. About 58,000 residents lost power during the storm.

The Los Gatos RAWS reported a wind gust to 68 mph at 8:32 a.m. PDT. Also, fierce winds downed trees on Rapley Ranch Road near State Route 35, on State Route 35 near Mountain House Restaurant in Kings Mountain, and along State Route 84 at the junction of State Route 35.

At 7:47 a.m. PDT the California Highway Patrol responded to a three car collision on Highway 1 at Devil's Slide.  Heavy rain and strong winds were a contributing factor of the crash. A 74-year-old woman lost her life in the accident.
The westbound lane of Highway 84 one half mile east of the La Honda Fire Station experienced a rock slide.  A large amount of rocks covered the road causing the roadway to be unusable.
Approximately one foot of water was flowing in the slow lane of southbound US Highway 101 at Lily St.

This powerful rainstorm overwhelmed pipes and manholes in San Mateo, San Carlos and Millbrae causing over 127,000 gallons of untreated sewage to flow into the streets and creeks. Over 55,000 gallons made it all the way to the San Francisco Bay.

Eight families were evacuated from the Bisceglia Avenue apartment complex in Morgan Hill due to flooding.  More than a foot of standing water was in the recently renovated four ground floor apartments. The three foot high wall, built to stave off flood water, was unsuccessful.

Monterey Road between Third and Fourth Streets was submerged due to flooding.  Flood waters entered a restaurant on Fourth Street causing damage.  Streets were flooded throughout Morgan Hill with water as high as two feet is some locations. The city actually ran out of moveable flooded signs and barriers, unable to mark all flooded locations.  Here are some of the locations experiencing flooding:  south end of town near the Morgan Hill Post Office on Monterey Road; Fountain Avenue; Llagas Creek Road, Monterey Road north of Morgan Hill, near Cochrane Road; Old Monterey Road from Monterey to Llagas Roads; Butterfield Boulevard at several locations, including at San Pedro and Diana Avenues; Watsonville Road at Monterey Road; Monterey Road at Burnett Avenue; Tennant Avenue; and Wright Avenue from Del Monte to Hale Avenues. Also, a sewage pipe connecting Morgan Hill to the Gilroy sewage treatment plant backed up causing 40,000 gallons of raw sewage to spill into the Ludewig Ranch causing the cancellation of the Harvest Festival in San Martin, an event to raise funds and food for the homeless.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: A 40-foot acacia tree toppled onto a garage roof in Campbell on West Rincon Avenue. The 30-year-old tree became wedged between the roof and the second story and blocked the entire entrance to the home.  At the Blossom Hill Elementary School in Los Gatos, a row of young trees were broken and bent lying on the ground due to the strong wind. At the intersection of Highway 17 and Interstate 280 a tree fell blocking a lane of traffic. In Milpitas, a large tree landed on a house on the 1300 block of Lassen Avenue clipping on side of the house causing minor gutter and roof damage.

High tension power lines were knocked onto the roadway at the intersection of Trout Gulch Road and Valencia Street in Aptos due to high winds. In Watsonville, high winds ripped off several large tree limbs and downed power lines on Martinelli Street. A parked car was severely damaged when a huge limb fell on it shortly after 6:00 p.m. PDT, breaking the windows and smashing the roof. In Santa Cruz, the roof of a service station on Mission Street was torn apart by the high winds. Near the Wilder Ranch State Park a large Cypress tree fell across Highway One blocking both lanes of traffic.
Strawberry farmers in the Pajaro Valley lost a week's worth of harvest due to heavy rains. The fields were swamped, causing berries to become spoiled.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS OF SAN BENITO COUNTY AND INTERIOR MONTEREY COUNTY INCLUDING PINNACLES NATIONAL MONUMENT
events.event_narrative: High winds blew up to 68 miles per hour.  At the Hernandez RAWS the winds gusted to 63 mph at 10:07 a.m. PDT.A power emergency was declared by the California's Electricity Grid Manager after strong winds knocked down a high-voltage transmission line in San Benito County.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: High winds were reported in many locations in the Santa Lucia Mountains.  Here are a few of the reports:  At ten miles southeast of Cachagua a mesonet site recorded a peak gust of 81 mph at 8:01 a.m. PDT, at 4 miles north of the Pico Blanco Campground a trained spotter reported an estimated wind gust of 69 mph at 9:45 a.m. PDT, at Highlands Peak a peak gust of 62 mph was recorded at 1:40 p.m. PDT.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A trained spotter reported an estimated wind gust to 59 mph in Monterey. At Schulte Road near Highway 16 a large tree was blown over blocking the entire roadway. On Holman Highway near Skyline Drive a tree fell onto a County Office of Education bus. In Pacific Grove, power lines and trees were toppled. One tree fell and damaged two houses on Presidio Boulevard. In Carmel Highlands a large tree fell onto a car on Yankee Point Drive.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / ARROYO SECO / LAKE SAN ANTONIO
events.event_narrative: A 500-kilowatt power line about 20 miles east of Moss Landing was blown down around 1:30 p.m. PDT. In Salinas, on the Hartnell College campus, a 60-foot eucalyptus tree fell onto a car and blocked Villa Street at 4:30 a.m. PDT.  In total, about 100 locations were visited by city crews in order to cut or remove trees blocking roads and sidewalks. In Gonzales, several trees were blown down.
The Pacific Coast Christian Academy and Little Lamb Preschool flooded after Little Bear Creek breached its banks. At least one foot of standing water remained in the school through the evening.
At 6:50 p.m. PDT the Arroyo Seco Creek was nearly a foot over flood stage.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: At about 11:20 a.m. PDT a 75-ffot eucalyptus tree fell onto a townhouse complex in East San Jose along the 2900 block of Rose Avenue causing substantial damage.
A 150-foot redwood tree was toppled by high winds.  It fell onto a home and damaged a car. The tree was planted in 1927.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Mount Diablo RAWS reported a peak gust of 58 mph at 1217 a.m. PDT while Los Vaqueros reported a peak gust of 60 mph at 9:45 p.m. PDT.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Choppy sea conditions and foggy weather were blamed for causing a wooden-hulled 20-foot boat to capsize near Bodega Bay.  An elderly husband and wife team had launched their motorized boat near Salmon Creek around 6:30 in the morning.  Several hours later their bodies were discovered, one near the broken bow of their boat, the other about one mile south of Salmon Creek.

A sailboat in rough waters just south of Pillar Point capsized causing two men to enter the ocean. One man was rescued quickly while the other was not removed from the water until an hour after the mishap.  He was pronounced dead by local paramedics.

Strong winds brought trees and tree branches down onto vehicles, into streets and onto power lines causing damage across the city of Napa. Down power lines sparked a vehicle fire near Jordan Lane and Lincoln Avenue and an entertainment center on the front porch of a home on the 100 block of Reed Circle caught fire. A Washington Pine tree sheared off and landed in a swimming pool.

Strong winds knocked trees and power lines down in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Reports of power outages and road closures due to down trees and power lines occurred in the San Lorenzo Valley, Bonny Doon and the Summit areas.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Measures peak wind gusts observed at RAWS:  Mallory Ridge, elevation 1760 feet - 63 mph at 8:45 a.m.; Diablo, elevation 3849 feet - 72 mph at 10:17 p.m.; and Poverty, elevation 2066 feet - 61 mph at 12:18 a.m.

A cold winter storm caused snow to fall in San Francisco's East Bay valleys as low as 350 feet above sea level. Locations such as Clayton, Alamo, Orinda, Moraga, Danville, Lamorinda, and the Livermore Valley all reported snow. It may have only been two inches at most, but it was enough to play in and cause some traffic problems.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Black ice and unsafe speed led to a single-car crash which killed the driver, the only occupant. The crash occurred in San Jose on southbound Almaden Expressway between Curtner Avenue and Canoas Garden Avenue. The police received the report of the mishap at 5:50 a.m. PST. and the man was pronounced dead at the scene. Elsewhere, the connector ramp from Highway 101 to Interstate 280 in San Jose was closed at 6:15 a.m. PST for about 90 minutes due to severe ice on the roadway. Even the light rail trains were delayed due to buildup of ice on the overhead wires used to power the trains. At Mineta San Jose International Airport flights were delayed for two hours as crews waited for frost on the airplanes to melt. There is only one airline at this airport that has deicing equipment.

Freezing conditions lingering from a winter storm that passed through northern and central California caused black ice to form on roadways in the Santa Cruz Mountains. The southbound lane of Highway 17 near Bear Creek Road was closed due to black ice.

The cold snap of December 7 and 8 was most likely a contributor to a century-old iron pipe water main failure. It resulted in opening a 20-by-20 foot sinkhole and flooding nearby intersections and a business at Division Street and Tenth Street in San Francisco's South of Market neighborhood on the night of December 11.

High surf caused erosion of cliffs in Pacifica resulting in an evacuation of an apartment building. About twenty tenants left their homes after city officials red-tagged the apartment building due to parts of the cliff falling into the ocean. Portions of the bluff lost up to 20 feet, leaving only 10 feet of land between the building and the sea.
An extreme astronomical high tide of seven and one tenth feet above mean sea level caused flooding, and the closure, of State Route One at the junction of US Highway 101 for about three hours.

Heavy surf from storms occurring this autumn and winter had finally eroded away the 30-foot bluff protecting San Francisco's Great Highway. The erosion removed the ground from beneath the guard rail of the southbound lanes causing the closure of all southbound lanes. The entire Great Highway was closed from Lincoln Way to Sloat Blvd. A request for a Governor's State of Emergency Proclamation was submitted in order to receive Emergency Relief funding from the Federal Highway Administration. The emergency, temporary estimate to repair the damage is $2.92 million dollars. However, a semi-permanent repair is estimated at an additional $15 million dollars.

Heavy surf combined with wind and rain to damage three docks in San Francisco. Pier 80, Dry Dock number one, began to sink due to hole in the hull allowing 700 gallons of water per minute into the dock. At Pier 45, the USS Pampanito's stern anchor chain snapped due to the rough seas and strong wind causing damage to the pier. And, at Pier 1.5, a 20 foot section of the Water Taxi Dock separated from the rest of the dock. Ferry Service on the San Francisco Bay was canceled due to the strong winds and large wind waves.

Heavy Rain led to flooding along the north and southbound lanes of US Highway 101 in the vicinity of McKee Road. At least one foot of standing water was reported near the railroad crossing requiring closure of the third and fourth southbound lanes. Also, one foot of standing water was reported in the third and fourth northbound lanes just south of McKee Road.
Heavy Rain led to flooding along the northbound lanes of US Highway 101 at Lafayette Street. The third and fourth lanes were closed causing traffic delays.
Heavy rain led to flooding in the southbound lanes of State Route 17 in the vicinity of Hamilton Avenue. At least one lane of traffic was closed.
Heavy Rain led to flooding along the southbound lanes of Interstate Highway 880 just north of Stevens Creek Boulevard. The middle and slow lanes were flooded with water at a depth of one foot.

Strong winds during the morning knocked down trees and power lines in numerous places in the Santa Cruz Mountains. In Ben Lomond, trees toppled and knocked down power lines on Alba Road; in Felton, power lines were knocked down at the intersection of Felton Empire Road and Graham Hill Road; in Boulder Creek, State Route 236 was closed just west of State Route 9 due to trees in the roadway; and in Bonny Doon, windblown trees knocked down power lines at Empire Grade Road and brought trees down at the intersection of Pine Flat Road and Bonny Doon Road. About 2,000 customers were without power in Santa Cruz County.

Strong wind uprooted a large oak tree forcing it onto Bennett Valley Road near Enterprise Road in the hills east of Petaluma partially blocking one lane of traffic.  The roots had grown under the roadway and when they were torn out of the ground they took about 7 inches of asphalt with them leading to the closure of the eastbound lane. Also in the hills east of Petaluma, another tree was reported to be uprooted on Sonoma Mountain Road at Pressley Road. Power outages across central Sonoma County numbered 3,584 customers.

Heavy rain combined with strong winds brought several large trees down across Santa Cruz County. In Watsonville, a eucalyptus tree was forced down bringing power lines down with it and damaging several utility poles in the process. A section of the tree blocked both lanes of Murphy Road between San Juan Road and Riverside Drive. In Santa Cruz, a pair of trees was toppled on First Street blocking lanes of traffic; and on Plateau Avenue a tree was blown down onto a car causing minor damage. About 2,000 customers were without power in Santa Cruz County.
Strong winds knocked down an oak tree in Healdsburg along Fitch Mountain Road. Power outages across central Sonoma County, including Santa Rosa, numbered 3,584 customers.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds knocked down trees on Bean Avenue at State Route One near Salmon Creek and on Bodega Highway near State Route One.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: High winds combined with heavy rain caused trees and power lines to fall across the coastal sections of Monterey County. In Carmel, a large tree limb broke free and damaged a car; on Rio Vista Drive near the mouth of Carmel Valley, a Monterey pine tree was knocked over causing the closure of the road; and another vehicle was damaged due to tree debris on Santa Lucia Avenue. In Pebble Beach a power pole was knocked down on Padre Lane blocking the roadway. Other weather related power problems occurred causing nearly 1,500 customers to lose electricity in Monterey County. A mesonet site at Point Sur Light Station reported an estimated gust to 62 mph at 10:00 a.m. PST. The Monterey Peninsula Airport reported a wind gust to 52 mph at 10:41 a.m. PST.
Squall line thunderstorms moved across the San Francisco International Airport producing wind gusts to 59 mph.

High wind knocked over power poles along San Mateo County's coast causing 12,000 customers to lose power. Downed power lines were reported in Half Moon Bay, at the intersection of Cedar and Acacia Avenues, along the 700 block on Main Street, and at Park Avenue in Moss Beach; and in Pacifica. The wind also caused damage to fixtures on the roof at the Half Moon Bay City Hall, and it dislodged a patio roof behind Sam's Chowder House, damaging solar panels used to power the restaurant. The Half Moon Airport mesonet site reported a wind gust of 69 mph at 10:00 a.m. PST. At least 12,000 customers lost power in San Mateo County.

Strong winds knocked over power poles along San Mateo County's bay shore line. Downed power lines were reported in San Mateo, on Cottage Grove Avenue; in Redwood City; and in Burlingame. Also, in Menlo Park, a man was hospitalized after a tree limb hit his car, causing him to crash. About 12,000 customers in San Mateo County were without power.

A microburst interrupted a passenger airliner's approach into San Francisco International Airport. After the 140 passenger jet encountered the microburst it diverted to and landed safely at the San Jose International Airport.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: The Bay Area Air Quality Management District's Kregor Peak mesonet site reported a peak wind gust of 77 mph at 8:00 a.m. PST. The Oakland North RAWS site reported a peak wind gust of 55 mph at 7:00 a.m. PST. And, the Las Trampas RAWS site reported a peak wind gust of 54 mph at 9:00 a.m. PST.
The Spring Valley RAWS site reported a peak wind gust of 73 mph at 6:00 a.m. PST. And, the Pigeon Point automated site reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 5:00 a.m. PST.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: The mesonet site at the Point Reyes Light Station reported a peak wind gust of 73 mph at 5:00 a.m. PST. And, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District's Valley Ford mesonet site site reported a peak wind gust of 50 mph at 5:00 a.m. PST.

The mesonet site at Twin Peaks reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 5:00 a.m. PST. And, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District's Fort Funston mesonet site reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph at 6:00 a.m. PST. The San Francisco Zoo decided to close because of numerous tree limbs scattered throughout the park. Minor flooding also occurred at the zoo.

High wind blew an oak tree down onto a car while a woman was driving it along Old La Honda Road near Woodside. The woman was unhurt and the car sustained minor damage. Also, in Woodside State Route 84 was closed at Grandview Drive due to downed trees. In Berkeley, power lines were blown down on the 1700 block of Oregon Street between Mc Gee Avenue and Grant Street. The ASOS at the San Francisco International Airport reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 6:09 a.m. PST. And, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District's Point San Pablo mesonet site reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 6:00 a.m. PST. Power outages occurred throughout the area forcing Canada College in Redwood City, the College of San Mateo and Stanford University to cancel classes.
The Bay Area Air Quality Management District's Sunol mesonet site reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 7:00 a.m. PST.

High winds brought an 18-inch diameter tree and power lines down along Lucas Valley Road about one-half mile east of Nicasio Valley Road blocking both lanes of traffic. In Monte Rio on Beach Avenue, two fir trees, one of them at least 100-foot tall, caused damage to a home, a pickup truck and a telephone substation. In Duncans Mills, a poplar tree fell into a home on Conifer Drive damaging the bedroom. The Hawkeye North RAWS site reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 5:00 a.m. PST.

Strong winds brought trees and power lines down at numerous locations in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Downed power lines and trees were reported at the intersection of State Route 9 and El Solyo Heights Road, which is located between Ben Lomond and Felton; in Ben Lomond at the intersection of State Route 9 and Glen Arbor Road; and in Felton at the Redwood Camp along East Zayante Road. In Scotts Valley, numerous trees and branches fell in Mission Springs crushing cars and damaging homes. The Ben Lomond RAWS site reported a peak wind gust of 51 mph at 6:00 a.m. PST. Around 4,000 customers lost power in the Santa Cruz Mountains.
Heavy rain caused two lanes of US Highway 101 to close near Paul Avenue due to flooding during the morning commute.
Heavy rain caused flooding within the Caldecott Tunnel of State Route 24 causing lanes of traffic to be closed at times along the northern most bore throughout the morning.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds knocked two trees down along East Santa Clara Street in San Jose. Around 10,000 customers lost power in the San Jose area.

Strong winds brought a tree down onto a car in the 400 block of Bellevue Street in Santa Cruz. Also in Santa Cruz, a 100-foot Monterey cypress tree on Clark Avenue came crashing down onto a car and clipped a house. The first floor TV and bath rooms were damaged. In Aptos, a redwood tree crashed into the road at Soquel Drive and Rio Del Mar Boulevard, which blocked both lanes making the road impassible. The mesonet site at the Long Marine Lab reported a peak wind gust of 51 mph at 7:00 a.m. PST. About 2,500 customers lost power in Santa Cruz County.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Near Clayton, a series of boulders loosened by the rain fell onto the intersection of March Creek and Morgan Territory Roads, damaging several vehicles. A similar slide occurred near Sunol on Niles Canyon Road, where mud and debris stopped three cars in their tracks.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds knocked a tree into high-voltage power lines in Orinda prompting a shelter in place order by the Sheriff's office.
Heavy rain led to flooding along the westbound lanes of Tenth Street near L Street in Antioch. Authorities closed the road.
Heavy rain led to flooding at and the closure of the Solari Street underpass of Tenth Street. Also, flooding was reported at Beacon Street between Eighth and Tenth Streets.
Heavy rain led to basement flooding of the Casa Zapata in Stern Hall, a dormitory on Stanford University in Palo Alto. Study rooms and the computer cluster were affected by the flooding.
Heavy rain caused flooding on and around State Highway One in Marin City. On and off ramps and most lanes of the highway were closed.
Heavy rain caused flooding on and around State Highway One in Larkspur. On and off ramps and most lanes of the highway were closed.
Heavy rain caused flooding at the intersection of Old Redwood Highway and Eastside Road just north of Windsor. The intersection was impassible.
Heavy rain caused flooding in Greenfield.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / ARROYO SECO / LAKE SAN ANTONIO
events.event_narrative: Strong winds uprooted a tree in King City causing damage to an apartment complex located in the 300 block of Russ Avenue.
Heavy rain caused flooding along State Highway 101 just north of Chualar. California Highway Patrol slowed traffic on Highway 101 because of the flooding.

Heavy rain caused the San Lorenzo River in Felton to rise over its banks and flood the Felton Grove community. Two hundred residents were called to evacuate before the river rose to 18 feet and overflowed into the streets, including River Road and Sylvan Way.
Heavy rain flooded the southbound lanes of US Highway 101 causing traffic to divert for over six hours.

Heavy rain caused Harbor Boulevard at the underpass of State Route 82 to flood submerging a car to the base of its windows. The road was barricaded to stop anyone else from driving into the water. Also in Belmont, a car repair business evacuated its building as 3 inches of water covered the floor. Belmont Creek was to blame.

Strong winds brought trees and power lines down across the San Francisco Bay Area. In Mipitas, a large tree was uprooted and blocked all lanes of traffic. In Richmond, part of a roof covering a YMCA swimming pool was blown off, scattering debris across Richmond Parkway resulting in its closure. In Palo Alto, saturated soils produce minor flooding and combined with high wind to bring a few trees down on the Palo Alto Golf Course.
