In Berkeley, power lines and trees were knocked down over the northern portion of the city near University Avenue and Martin Luther King Jr. Way. Also in Berkeley, winds toppled a tree onto the roof of a residence on the 2900 block of Sacramento Street. In Newark, a 50-foot tree fell near the intersection of Cedar and Newark Boulevards. In Menlo Park, a driver was injured when the top of a Redwood tree came crashing through his windshield as he was driving on Santa Cruz Avenue near Hillview Middle School.

As an arrest warrant was being served at a home in Campbell, a man ran into his backyard and hopped over a fence, where a cement drainage ditch was running at full capacity. The man tried to jump over the ditch but got caught in the water and dragged downstream. The Police Officers saw him try to keep his head above water, but he went under and drowned.

Heavy rain caused Pulgas Creek to overflow its banks and flood some classrooms at Central Middle School in San Carlos. Also, several streets were blocked off in low-lying areas just west of US Highway 101, including Taylor Avenue in San Carlos and parts of Rolison Road in Redwood City. In Atherton, officials closed March Road from Middlefield Road to Fair Oaks Avenue because a creek had begun to flood.

Strong winds and saturated soil combined to knock over a 50-foot Douglas fir tree along Turnagain Road in Kentfield. In Sonoma, a fallen tree smashed a home. In Santa Rosa, a tree crashed down onto a home on Proctor Drive rendering it uninhabitable. In Yountville a 150- to 200-year-old Coast Live Oak toppled next to a home on Humboldt Street causing damage to a fence. Also in Santa Rosa, A 50-foot-plus Cedar tree came down onto a home on Manor Drive damaging the back area of the house. Along State Route 12, a tree fell onto a moving vehicle just east of Glen Ellen causing closure of the roadway. In Sonoma, a redwood tree fell through the roof of the K building at Sonoma Valley High School. In Healdsburg, power lines fell along Alexander Valley Road.

Officials closed the southbound US Highway 101 off ramp to State Highway 37 and South Novato Boulevard due to flooding in Novato. Minor flooding occurred throughout Marin County and caused schools to close because of flooding concerns.

Heavy rain led to flooding of Sonoma Creek along State Route 121 near Schellville. Numerous roads were blocked throughout the region because of standing water. Daywalt, Green Valley, Mark West Station, Todd, Portal, Piner and Valley Ford-Freestone Roads were among the areas closed roads due to flooding. The heavy rains also infiltrated the sewer pipes in five places in Boyes Hot Springs and in Sonoma causing overflows into streets and creeks.

Strong winds toppled two large trees, a Coastal Redwood and a spruce, on Valley Avenue just west of Santa Rita Road in Pleasanton causing damage to a block wall. Also in Pleasanton, power lines were damaged by strong winds on Spring Street and on Valley Avenue. In Alamo, a centuries-old oak tree detached from its muddy soil and came to rest on a Deodar Lane home causing extensive damage. In Martinez, A tree fell along Alhambra Valley Road, between Castro Ranch and Bear Creek Road, taking power lines down with it. Also, in Orinda, power lines were blown down near La Espiral.
Heavy rain caused knee-deep flooding at the intersections of Second and Harrison Streets in Berkeley.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Strong winds knocked over numerous trees and power lines along the Coast of Monterey County. In Pacific Grove a pine tree fell onto a house along Sunset Drive. In Monterey, a pine tree fell onto an apartment building along Dela Vina Avenue and damaged a single-family home next door as the root ball was ripped out of the ground. In Carmel-By-The-Sea, Junipero Street was closed between Tenth and Eleventh Avenues for about two hours after a tree fell bringing power lines down with it.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind brought a number of trees and tree limbs down across San Jose. On Cherry Lane an 80-foot cedar tree toppled over, taking down a telephone pole and two transformers along with it. The tree fell across the street damaging a vehicle on the other side. In Los Gatos, trees fell on Shady Lane just east of Short Road and near the intersection of Harwood and Blossom Hill Roads.

Stong winds brought trees down in Watsonville. A house on the 300 block of Manfre Road was damaged by a redwood tree, and a large cypress tree damged a home and a car on Clifford Drive near Melrose Avenue.
State Highway 17 was closed for about three hours due to flooding.
Strong wind brought trees and power lines down onto State Route One just north of the Santa Cruz and San Mateo county line. The road was closed for two hours.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Damaging surf along Monterey counties coast has caused erosion concerns along State Highway One. About nine miles north of the San Luis Obispo county line, officials have closed the highway for night travel. At the opening of the Carmel River, high waves pushed sand and debris across the State Beach parking lot, caused a portion of the bluff supporting Scenic Road to slump, and have eroded the terrace bluff south of the lagoon damaging the stairway.
Rescuers pulled six people out of cars that stalled in 3-foot water in Pescadero.
A RAWS site at Spring Valley reported a wind gust to 64 mph at 9:19 a.m. PST.
An intense hail storm occurred near Ryan Ranch just south-southeast of Del Rey Oaks.
A hail storm occurred in the mountains of Santa Cruz County. A report of one inch diameter hail came from a motorist traveling along Eureka canyon Road north of Corralitos.

High surf caused an 80-foot-wide and 20-foot deep chunk of land to erode into the ocean in Pacifica at 5 a.m. on January 21. Residents of six apartment units were evacuated as the cliff eroded up to their back porches. The owners of the apartments are attempting to strengthen the cliff and save the apartments from succumbing to the same fate as the previous cliff face. So far they have spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on this project.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind blew down a 60-foot tree onto the cab of a pickup truck in downtown San Jose. A two-year-old in the truck was killed. The remaining two family members were uninjured. The incident occurred on Seventh Street near Market Street.
Strong wind caused several large trees to fall into the roadway along State route 84 near Woodside. A half-mile stretch of the highway was closed for part of the day to remove the trees.
Strong wind knocked down a large tree in Pleasant Hill onto a parked car. The incident occurred in the 1700 block of Lucille Lane.

A low topped super cell produced an EF0 tornado near Brentwood. The tornado crossed power lines and destroyed a utility pole (DI24, DOD4). An eyewitness described the tornado as high winds from swirling white cloud. The pole was twisted to the ground and the top one-third of the 40-foot pole was splintered. Fifty-five customers lost power at 12:54 p.m. PST.

Strong wind brought down a large oak tree along Fitch Mountain Road in Healdsburg. The tree smashed into a home and caused the road to be closed. Some of the other areas experienced downed trees and power lines were Sebastopol, Forestville and Santa Rosa. In all, around 1,200 customers were without power.

Strong wind knocked down a huge oak tree over the 1200 block of Eureka Canyon Road. The tree, with a five-foot diameter base, tore out power lines in several places, forcing officials to close the road for most of the day. Residents in the area, about 115, lost power.

A motorist decided to drive around barriers stating the road was flooded and ended up submerged up to his door handles. Atascadero Creek was running three feet deep across Green Valley Road in Graton when the driver decided to attempt to cross the creek. Other commonly flooded roads in Sonoma County remained closed.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: As the area began to dry out from the parade of storms in January, the lingering effects caused a large tree to succumb to the weight of the rain it absorbed. The 100-year old tree fell onto three pedestrians. Two women and a man walking on the sidewalk were struck and injured by the trees branches. The oak tree was located at Mary Avenue and Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino.
Brief heavy rain combined with strong wind to topple a pepperwood tree into power lines on Fitch Mountain Road in Healdsburg cutting power to 462 residents.

Brief heavy rain combined with strong wind to knock over a cypress tree onto Alta Drive in Aptos.  Several other trees were toppled across Santa Cruz County.  Also, a few minor rockslides and mudslides were reported.

Strong wind combined with brief heavy rain to cause trees, tree limbs and power lines to fall. At the height of the storm, around 1:30 p.m. PST, 4,350 customers were without power in San Francisco's East Bay.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Two men entered the water at Carmel Beach and one man was swept out to sea by a rip current. The 34-year-old man's body was never found and he was presumed drowned. High surf was occurring at the time under a sunny sky.

The Mavericks Big Wave Surf Contest is an annual event that occurs during the winter time when significantly high surf is happening under a partly cloudy to sunny sky. During the event a set of sneaker waves washed onto the shore were numerous spectators were enjoying the contest. When the sneaker waves inundated the previously dry spectator area they knocked at least 40 off their feet and injured at least 13. The most serious injuries were broken bones. Three people were taken to the hospital while many were treated for hyperthermia. Also damaged in the inundation were video and audio equipment used during the contest.

A rain-slicked road led to the crash of a car at the intersection of Mount Diablo Boulevard and Iron Horse Regional Trail in Walnut Creek. The vehicle crashed through a fence and landed upside down in the rain-swollen San Ramon Creek bypass. The driver and one other individual perished, while one occupant was rescued three miles downstream. A Contra Costa County official stated that at the time of the crash, the water would have been 2.34 feet deep and flowing at 6.4 feet per second.
Heavy rain caused flooding at the intersection of Wilson Hill and Marshall Petaluma Roads.  Mud consumed the westbound lane and a large tree fell onto the roadway.

At approximately 11:36 p.m. on Sunday, State Route 236 was closed from 1.6 to 1.9 miles north of the junction of State Route 9 due to a downed tree and power lines.  The route reopened at approximately noon the next day.

A debris flow initiated in a seasonal stream bed rushing hundreds of feet downhill into a driveway and home on Upper Highland Road near Eureka Canyon Road.  A car and one side of a home were buried in about nine feet of rock, dirt, wood chunks and water.  The home was severely damaged and deemed unsafe and uninhabitable. Over thirty Santa Cruz county roads were closed and damaged in flash flooding and debris flows in the Santa Cruz Mountains.  Two people were rescued from a vehicle when they got stuck in water along Eureka Canyon Road.
A debris flow closed both lanes of Highway 1 at mile marker 37 around 4:15 p.m. PDT.  Also, some flooding occurred along the Big Sur River.

A severely damaged thirty foot sailing vessel was found abandoned by its occupants near Seal Rocks, San Francisco, California.  The vessel had water in it and all of the windows had been blown out as if hit by a large wave.  The couple who were on board perished in the accident.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A 24-foot motorized fishing boat capsized in the six to eight foot surf about one mile offshore of Ten Mile Beach, also known as The Great Beach, north of Point Reyes. The four fishermen aboard lost their lives as they were thrown into the frigid water.  None of them were wearing life vests. Also, the boat was totally destroyed with parts of the boat washing up along more than one mile of shoreline.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: As many as ten people at Monastery Beach, south of Carmel, were caught by surprise as a sneaker wave washed them from the beach into the ocean. A Good Samaritan decided to help with the rescue and died after pulling at least one person to safety. Another beachgoer succumbed to injuries and died the next day. Five others were taken to local hospitals and then released.

Strong wind combined with heavy rain to topple trees and power lines causing road closures and power outages. In San Francisco's North Bay Area nearly 10,000 customers lost power due to trees falling onto power lines. West of the city of Napa a large redwood tree with a four foot diameter trunk fell onto power lines and across Redwood Road. In Fairfax, trees fell near the intersection of Mora Avenue and Buena Vista Avenue. And, in Chileno Valley, trees fell near the intersection of Fallon-Two Rock Road and Twin Bridge Road. Numerous other incidents of trees blocking roadways were reported in Napa and Marin counties. Also of note, the storm caused a construction barge in the bay near Paradise Cay to list.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind combined with heavy rain to topple trees and power lines causing road closures and power outages. In San Francisco's North Bay Area nearly 10,000 customers lost power due to trees falling onto power lines. In one instance, a tree knocked down a power line when it fell in Inverness Park near the intersection of Portola Avenue and Vallejo Avenue.
Heavy rain caused rocks to fall onto State Highway 128 near Monticello dam at Lake Berryessa partially blocking the roadway.

Heavy rain led to flooding on State Highway 29 under Trancas Street. Three vehicles crashed after losing control in the flooded underpass. Two of the vehicles collided while the other ran into a guard rail. No one was hurt.
Heavy rain led to a small mudslide behind a house on Oakdale Avenue near Sausalito Street in Corte Madera.
Heavy rain led to a small mudslide on River Road near Boyes Hot Springs, minor flooding along United States Highway 101 in Cotati and minor flooding on State Highway 12.
Heavy rain caused a small debris slide to occur along State Highway 1 just north of Jenner.

Strong winds and heavy rain caused a power substation to fail leading to more than 15,000 customers to lose power in Oakland, Alameda and surrounding communities. The Twelfth Street BART station in downtown Oakland was shut down because of the power outage. The power failed around 2:15 p.m. PST.

Heavy rain led to minor flooding of westbound Interstate 580 west of State Highway 24. An inch of water spread into about five feet of the right-hand lane. Also, The High Street on-ramp to northbound Interstate 880 was flooded due to poor drainage.

Strong winds caused power lines to fall at approximately 5:51 p.m. PST along State Route 84.  The route was closed at the Junction of State Route 35 in Woodside due to the downed power lines. The route reopened at 7:52 p.m. PST on Monday, October 25.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Two women were swept into the ocean by a sneaker wave at Carmel River Beach and taken out to sea by a rip current around 3:15 p.m. PST. One woman perished in the ocean and the other was rescued.

Strong winds combined with heavy rain dropped trees onto buildings, pushed cars off roads and caused power outages across the area. Power lines were knocked to the ground around 6:23 p.m. PST in the area of Empire Grade and Ice Cream Grade causing 800 customers to lose power. A total of 1100 customers lost power in Santa Cruz County. In another spot along Empire Grade downed power lines and trees blocked the entire road north of Smith Grade. Power lines also fell into trees along Lompico Road around 7 p.m. PST sparking a small fire. Power lines even fell onto a car on State Route 9 at Henry Cowell State Park around 7 p.m. PST.  In Felton around 7:15 p.m. PST a tree fell through the roof of a home on Buckeye Drive. The greatest damage occurred around 7:20 pm. PST when large trees fell into buildings in Mount Herman. Sequoia Lodge, an eight room facility, and a three-room cabin were significantly damaged when five foot diameter trees were uprooted by the strong winds.

Strong winds combined with heavy rain to cause power lines and trees to fall. The intersection of Graham Hill Road at Tanner Heights near Santa Cruz was closed after a live power line landed in the road. In all, Santa Cruz County experienced power outages to about 1100 customers.

Heavy rain combined with strong wind to cause numerous trees to fall down. On Porter Creek Road at about 5 a.m. PST a tree blew onto a passing car and knocked power lines down causing the road to be closed. On Graton Road at Upp Road another tree was blown onto power lines blocking the road in both directions. Additional trees were reported down on Martinelli Road about 7:15 a.m. and on Harrison Grade Road around 11:25 a.m.  In all, about 2,200 customers lost power in the North Bay from this storm.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: At approximately 5:14 a.m. PST State Route 1 was closed 5.7 miles south of the junction of US 101 due to a mudslide. The roadway reopened at 6:58 a.m.
Brief heavy rain fell onto saturated soil causing a minor debris flow to occur along Old San Jose Road. The southbound lane was blocked by mud and debris near the Subud Center.
Brief heavy rain fell onto saturated soil causing a minor debris flow to occur along Soquel San Jose Road. The northbound lane was blocked by mud and debris near Miller Cut-Off.

Many trees were blown down across Santa Cruz County, some causing power outages. In particular, a large Acacia tree was blown over about 10:30 a.m. PST causing a section of Freedom Boulevard between Hames and Pleasant Valley roads to shut down. Around 400 homes and businesses lost power early Sunday morning.

Many trees were blown down across Santa Cruz County, some causing power outages. In particular, a large tree was blown onto Highway 9 in Boulder Creek, which slowed vehicle traffic until crews removed it. Also, power lines were blown down around 9:45 a.m. PST in Woodside causing the closure of State Route 84 at Grandview Road. At approximately 12:42 p.m. PST State Route 35 was closed 2.2 miles north of the Junction of State Route 9 due to downed power lines.

Two Valley Oak trees, next to each other, were blown down in Cloverdale. The two trees were estimated to be over 100 years old and were between 70 and 80 feet tall. There were no injuries; however, the Snack Shack and an adjacent building sustained damage.

Strong wind combined with heavy rain to force a substantial oak tree to fall at the Hotel Yountville in Yountville Sunday afternoon. The Oak tree was to have been a major focus of the landscaping plan. The tree fell onto a new rock wall and damaged a pump house.

Heavy rain caused a minor slide in San Anselmo that resulted in a grove of Eucalyptus trees becoming unstable behind a business on Red Hill Avenue. At least one tree fell over and damaged the business's building.
Strong wind caused a large tree to tumble onto State Route 35 near John Daly Road in Daly City. The road was closed at 1:07 a.m. PST.
Strong wind caused a four to five foot diameter Douglas fir tree to fall into State Route 9 just south of Glengarry Road in the Santa Cruz area. The road was closed from 4:46 p.m. to 6:32 p.m. PST.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Rain over the previous twelve hours caused the saturated soil along State Highway 1 at Stinson Beach to form a minor landslide. The highway was closed from 2:12 p.m. to 5:11 p.m. PST.
Strong wind brought down trees and power lines in Santa Cruz resulting in closure of State Route 9 just south of Pacific Avenue. The highway was closed from approximately 5:48 p.m. to 10:19 p.m. PST.

Damaging wind brought a tree down onto State Route 9 causing its closure from one mile south to 2.9 miles south of the south Junction of State Route 236. The Highway was closed from 6:20 p.m. to 10:29 p.m. PST.

Brief heavy rain on saturated soil caused a mud slide along State Route 1 in the Devil's Slide area. The road was closed from 6.7 miles north of Half Moon Bay to 2.3 miles south of Pacifica from 11:05 p.m. to 5:29 a.m. PST the next day.

Strong wind blew down a sixty-foot Pine tree which snagged a power line before crashing down onto a pickup truck on Midway Boulevard in Novato. The incident cut power to nearly 3,000 households. Other trees fell, with local power outages reported in San Anselmo, Fairfax, Corte Madera, San Rafael, Kentfield and Bolinas.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Strong wind and saturated soil caused trees to be uprooted in portions of the northern Big Sur coast and near Monterey. In Carmel Highlands, a tree was blown onto a house causing some damage. In the Monterey area wind removed tree branches which severed power lines resulting in numerous power outages across the peninsula. In all, more than 10,600 customers lost power.

Strong wind caused a double-trunked, 100 foot tall Oak tree to snap at its base and fall onto an occupied cabin-like tent near Mark West Springs. A seven-year-old girl and her grandmother were playing as the tree crashed to the ground resulting in the death of the 70-year-old woman. The girl was not physically injured.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind brought several trees down throughout Sonoma County with several falling across Highway 1 near Sea Ranch.

Large waves pounded the central California coast causing chunks of the cliffs in Pacifica to fall into the ocean. The two, now vacant, apartment houses which had their foundation undermined last winter are now even closer to falling into the ocean as nature eats away at the cliffs supporting them. About one-third of the apartment buildings are unsupported and hanging over the cliffs.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Strong wind knocked over a large Monterey pine in the area of Josselyn Canyon Road and Wagon Wheel Drive. The tree fell around 6:00 p.m. PST and damaged a power pole. About 20 minutes later, another pine tree fell nearby on Twin Oaks Drive, landing on an unoccupied sport utility vehicle. Both pine trees were about 100 feet tall.

Dozens of trees were knocked down in Sonoma County as strong wind combined with saturated soil. In particular, a man was injured and his vehicle severely damaged when a large tree and power lines fell onto his car shortly after 7:00 a.m. PST.

Strong wind knocked down a power pole and transformer onto an Oakley house on Arminio Lane around 9:50 a.m. PST. Elsewhere in Oakley, a six-foot diameter eucalyptus tree was uprooted by the wind and fell onto the empty cab of a big-rig truck. As it was going down it clipped the side of a house in the 2400 block of Delta Road.
Strong wind caused a large tree to topple onto power lines on the 600 block of Bonita Drive in Aptos around 3:00 p.m. PST.
A large tree fell on an occupied vehicle causing the closure of State Route 183 in the Monterey Area at approximately 9:21 p.m. PST. The roadway was reopened at 10:57 p.m.

At approximately 3:30 a.m. PST on January 1, 2011 State Route 29 was closed from St. Helena (Napa County) to the Napa/Lake County line due to snow. The roadway reopened at 7:12 a.m. PST on January 1, 2011.

At approximately 5:00 p.m. PST, State Route 9 at Scenic Way, in the Santa Cruz area, was closed due to downed trees and power lines. The roadway reopened on January 3, 2011, at approximately 6:21 a.m.
At approximately 5:04 p.m. PST State Route 9 was closed from 1.2 miles north of Felton to 2.4 miles north of Felton due to downed power lines. The roadway reopened at 5:56 a.m. on January 3, 2011.

Black ice made rural roads treacherous, including Porter Creek Road, where a car slid, flipped and finally smashed into a bedroom wall of a home. There were two other accidents due to black ice on roadways.
A tree felled by high winds crushed a car in Oakland during the early morning hours.
A thirty year old male big-wave surfer was injured attempting to surf at Mavericks, a well known big wave surf area 25 miles south of San Francisco near Half Moon Bay.

Strong and gusty northerly wind caused numerous trees and power lines to topple in Santa Cruz County. An acacia tree was knocked over at 10:10 a.m. PST on the 700 block of Amesti Road in Watsonville. A pine tree fell in the northbound lanes of Highway 1 just north of Park Avenue about 10:45 a.m. PST causing traffic to backup for more than a mile. Downed trees were also reported just after 11:00 a.m. PST at the 400 block of Roxas Street in Santa Cruz, the 800 block of 35th Avenue in Live Oak, and at Clares Street and Wharf Road in Capitola. The wind also snapped a power pole on Clares Street in Capitola.

Pre-dawn downpours caused localized small stream flooding in some areas in central Sonoma County. Those of note were Todd Road west of Stony Point Road outside of Santa Rosa, and Green Hill Road near Ross Road in Granton, where a man drove into the high water and became stuck for a time just after 7:00 a.m. PST. Flooding also caused the closure of Green Valley Road near Sullivan Road, where another vehicle stalled in the high water, and made a pond out of Shiloh Road near Windsor Road. Minor rock and mud slides were reported throughout the area between Santa Rosa and Calistoga.

Strong and gusty wind developed ahead of a long wave trough. Southwest to west wind began to increase during the afternoon and peaked in the evening. A trained weather spotter reported a measured wind gust of 60 MPH at 6:15 p.m. PST. Other automated observation systems around the area above 1,000 feet in elevation reported gusts up to 83 MPH. The wind caused large trees and power lines to fall. Also, road closures occurred due to the downed trees and power lines. Of note, Porter Creek Road was closed until 3:00 p.m. Wednesday due to the efforts of removing a large tree that fell across the roadway. Overall, more than a dozen power poles were pushed down in Marin County.

Strong and gusty wind developed ahead of a long wave trough. Southwest to west wind began to increase late in the afternoon and peaked in the late evening. A mesonet automated weather reporting system measured a wind gust of 60 MPH at midnight. Other automated observation systems around the area above 1,000 feet in elevation reported gusts up to 83 MPH. The wind caused large trees and power lines to fall. Also, road closures occurred due to the downed trees and power lines. Of note, a tree fell onto a house on Alta Avenue in Piedmont. Overall, more than 6,500 customers lost power in the San Francisco Bay Area.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: High tide combined with rain runoff to cause tidal flooding in Mill Valley. The Park and Ride at Highway 101 and Shoreline Highway was impacted by the high water. The high tide at Sausalito reached 6.4 feet around 9:33 a.m. PST.

Strong and gusty wind knocked over an 80 foot tall Monterey pine tree onto two fifth-wheel trailers around 10:00 a.m. PST at the New Brighton State Beach campground. The trailers were destroyed and there were no injuries. More trees and also power lines were downed in and around Santa Cruz. At Santa Cruz and Centennial Streets around noon power lines fell causing power outages.

Heavy rain led to small stream flooding and minor rock slides in Santa Cruz County. Near Riverdale Boulevard north of Boulder Creek, water washed over a bridge at Highway 9 around 8:40 a.m. PST. Around 2:00 p.m. PST a minor rock slide was reported near Laurel Glen and Soquel San Jose Roads. And, about 3:50 p.m. PST another rock slide occurred on Highway 129 at Rogge Lane near Watsonville, which stopped traffic.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds and rough seas combined to cause a 15-foot boat to capsize near Bodega Bay resulting in the death of a 65 year-old man.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A 51 year-old woman walking with her husband at Portuguese Beach in Bodega Bay attempted to rescue their dog from the surf. During the rescue attempt the woman was caught in the surf herself and swept into the water. The waves were reported to be up to ten feet. Both the woman and her dog drowned.

Strong and gusty wind caused trees and power lines to fall resulting in several hundred customers to lose power and about a half-dozen roads to close. Of significance was an oak tree that damaged a vehicle as it was knocked over by the wind around 6:30 p.m. PST on River Road near Trenton Healdsburg Road.
Gusty wind caused a tree to fall onto the westbound connector of State Route 4 to westbound Interstate 80 at approximately 5:05 a.m. PST. The roadway reopened at 7:00 a.m. PST.

After four days of rain with over seven inches falling in the higher terrain, the Willow Brook Creek swelled beyond its banks causing minor flooding along its channel. The stream gages at Old Redwood Highway and Penngrove Park went over their flood stages.

Heavy rain drenched San Francisco causing storm drains to back up which resulted in minor flooding throughout the city. The Public Utilities Commission reported 25 minor floods at various locations. Nineteen of those floods occurred at intersections and six occurred at homes or businesses.
Heavy rain caused a landslide to occur around 3:18 a.m. PST along State Route 84 at Portola Road in Woodside.  The roadway reopened at 4:16 a.m. PST.

Strong wind combined with rain soaked soil to knock trees and power poles down. At approximately 9:15 a.m. PST power lines fell across State Route 84 at the junction of State Route 85 in Woodside. The roadway was reopened at 4:56 p.m. PST.
Strong wind combined with rain soaked soil to knock trees and power poles down. A large tree fell onto power lines in the 1100 block of Bromfield Road in Woodside causing the closure of the roadway.

Strong wind combined with rain soaked soil to knock trees and power poles down. A giant eucalyptus tree collapsed on the front entrance to a house. The tree also smashed two cars and severed power lines.

A tsunami impacted Santa Cruz...in particular Santa Cruz Harbor. Impacts included: eighteen vessels sunk, four vessels capsized, 100+ vessels with either superficial damage or waiting to be assessed, oil sheen on the water and serious damage to harbor facilities.
A tsunami affected the San Mateo County coast. A preliminary damage assessment was conducted due to the response, but no physical damage reported.
At the Berkeley Marina the tsunami damaged six boat slips, three docks, and snapped a wooden piling.
High winds sheared off more than a dozen trees along a short stretch of Tomales-Petaluma Road.
Heavy rain overwhelmed a drainage pipe that runs underneath Pacific Cove Mobile Home Park, and then cascaded down Riverview Drive into the village causing damage to homes and businesses.
There were 1279 acres of crops or croplands impacted by flooding from the Salinas River and its tributaries (1263 acres of Salinas River acreage and 16 acres from the tributaries).

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A rock and mud slide closed Highway 1 south of Big Sur, just south of Limekiln Creek.

Officials in Santa Cruz County are estimating that heavy rain caused $8.3 million in damage to unincorporated areas of the County, including a slide near Scotts Valley that cut off access to more than 30 homes. Damage to the City of Santa Cruz is estimated at $1.5 million.

Heavy rain caused numerous slides as well as downed trees and power lines. On March 24 the following areas were affected: Alta Via Road at Moonridge was closed because of a mudslide; Blue Ridge Drive was closed because of downed wires; Buzzard Lagoon Road past address 117 was closed because of a mudslide with downed trees and wires; Eureka Canyon Road was closed because of downed trees and wires; Glenwood Drive at Weston Drive was closed because of a slide; Glenwood Drive at Northridge Drive was closed because of a downed tree and wires; Nelson Road at address 231 was closed because of a mudslide and downed tree; a tree fell on a car on East Zayante Road near Quail Hollow Road; a tree fell on a Jeep near La Madrona Road and Sims Drive; Trees were reported to have fallen into houses at 401 Aptos Creek Road, 523 Santa Margarita Drive and the 400 block of Monterey Drive, all in Aptos and at a house on Moran Way and East Cliff Drive in Live Oak.
A large tree fell and cleaved a house in two on the 400 block of Nelson Road outside Scotts Valley.
A 60 to 70 foot Fir tree crashed into the roof, punching holes through the ceiling.

A rock slide occurred above Nelson Road outside of Scotts Valley. Approximately 28 people live above the slide; however, no homes were, or will be threatened if the slide should continue. Rocks covered about 200 yards of roadway isolating the neighborhood.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Both directions of SR-1 at milepost 20.5, in the Monterey Area, were closed due to a mudslide.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: State Route 130 at Mt Hamilton Rd was closed 9 miles west of San Jose at Quimby Rd due to a rock slide.
Rain saturated Pleasanton Ridge slid causing a water main break leaving 160 residents without potable water.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Heavy rain and high surf caused widespread flooding, mudslides, road closures, and downed power lines across Monterey County.

In San Anselmo heavy rain and strong wind caused mudslides, trees to blow down and power poles to topple. The following are other damage reports from around the city. On Florence Road trees fell into the public right of way blocking the roadway and crushing a car. It also took down several PGE, cable and telephone poles. On Woodruff Ave, a mudslide traveled 1/4 mile down the road carrying structure debris and blocking a main intersection that accesses 12 homes.  On Scenic Ave, a mudslide entered a roadway and wind blew down a few power poles. At 29 Summit Ave, a mudslide closed roads; caused water, gas and sewer lines to break and took out numerous trees. On Redwood Rd, the road was damaged and even portions of the road collapse due to excess rain washing down hill. The roadway was closed between 390 and 405 Redwood Rd due to mudslide undermining the road.
Green Valley Road, west of Sullivan in the town of Graton was closed due to flooding. Mark West Station Road, at Starr Road in the town of Windsor was closed due to flooding.
Reports indicate that as many as fourteen sailboats and one houseboat floated free in Richardson Bay during the event with some becoming beached off Strawberry Point.
At 10:20 pm Saturday night a huge oak tree, six feet in diameter, fell onto a SUV killing a 46 year-old man.
An EF1 tornado completely destroyed a metal building and severely bent a metal gate.
A 35 year old welder from Hawaii died around 6 pm Wednesday in high surf. The wave faces reached heights of 40 to 45 feet on the biggest sets.
State Route 9 was closed to northbound traffic at the Junction of State Route 35 due to a mud slide. There was no information when the roadway was reopened.
State Route 121 was closed from the Junction of State Route 12 to Eighth Street in Schellville due to flooding. There is no information when the roadway reopened.
Mark West Station Road was closed at Starr Road due to flooding.
Millerick Road was closed due to flooding.
Sanford Road was closed at Occidental Road due to flooding.
Valley Ford Road was closed due to flooding between Bloomfield and Highway 1.

A landslide in the City of San Pablo affected six homes and two city parcels. The area affected was along Wyman Street and Hillcrest Road. Throughout Contra Costa County, nearly $16 million worth of damage occurred due to the March storms.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Heavy rain on saturated soils caused a large landslide on State Route One 13.7 miles north of Big Sur State Park at Rocky Creek. The roadway reopened to one-way controlled traffic on April 20, 2011.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A hillside south of Big Sur gave way weeks after the last heavy rainfall ended. A debris flow occurred 6.2 miles north of the San Luis Obispo County line along State Highway One. The road remained closed until June 9, 2011.

A hillside near the Watsonville airport gave way weeks after the last heavy rainfall ended. A debris flow occurred at Manfre Road in Freedom and entered a home. The home was destroyed along with everything in it when three feet of mud and debris filled the house.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Moss Landing Harbor sustained damages to docks and harbor structures during the tsunami.
A section of Pleasanton Ridge gave way when rain-saturated soil let damaging a water main pipe. The damage to the water main pipe left 160 residents without potable water.

events.cz_name: POINT REYES TO PIGEON POINT...OUT TO 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Strong wind and chaotic seas caused a sailboat to capsize in the water near San Francisco's Ocean Beach. One man was pulled from the water around 4:00 p.m. and the other man aboard was not found and presumed dead.

At approximately 2330 hours on May 17, 2011 US Highway 101 northbound connector to northbound SR 1 was closed due to flooding. The roadway reopened at 0325 hours on May 18, 2011. The flooding was due to Astronomical High Tide.

Torrential rains over San Francisco's North Bay hit vineyards at a critical time of the growing season, when many vines had opened their flowers to begin the delicate process of self-fertilization. Around 10 to 15 percent of crops were lost equating to tens of millions of dollars to Sonoma County farmers.

Heavy rain caused cherry crops in east Contra Costa County to absorb too much water resulting in splitting fruit. Split cherries are susceptible to bacteria and therefore can only be used in a limited capacity.
Strong wind combined with saturated soil to knock a giant oak tree to the ground at the Sonoma Development Center.

Heavy rain caused the flood control channel of the Gilroy creek near Forest Street to rise to near capacity. Just before noon firefighters and police arrived at the scene where they pulled a 43-year-old male from the water. His death was determined to be from drowning.
Pickup truck was struck by lightning. Electrical system was knocked out in the truck.
St Helena Rd, at Tarwater Rd, in Sonoma County was closed due to a down tree.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: At approximately 0930PST on November 24, 2011 northbound US 101 connector to northbound SR 1 was closed due to flooding. The roadway reopened at 1346 hours.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: At approximately 1030PST on November 25, 2011 northbound US 101 connector to northbound SR 1 was closed due to flooding. The roadway reopened at 1316 hours.

In Calistoga, CA emergency officials responded to nine calls between 2200 and 2300PST for wind damage. Damage included fallen trees, large tree limbs, and a metal awning ripped from a home in Chateau Calistoga Mobile Home Park.
A worker in a crane was burned around 1120PST Friday November 18, 2011 when a gust of wind blew him into a power line.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: A 35 year-old male wildlife biologist of Big Sur was killed by a falling tree during high winds. The tree toppled over at 1450PST Wednesday, November 30, 2011 near North Coast Road at mile marker 16.
High winds snapped a power pole on Old Redwood Highway in the Larkfield area north of Santa Rosa.
About 190 customers lost power when strong winds knocked a wire down around 1840PST near Hagan Road and Olive Hill Lane in Napa.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds toppled a tree across the northbound lanes of US 101 near SR 237 in Sunnyvale.
Strong winds knocked down trees and downed power lines in Corralitos between 1500 and 1900PST. Falling trees also took down a transmission line in the Scotts Valley area.
Winds gusted to 70 mph in the Santa Cruz Mountains downing trees and power lines. This included a critical transmission line near Castle Rock State Park.
Strong winds toppled trees and a few power lines across west Sonoma County.
Wind gusted to 54 mph at Chabot and 51 mph at Pt. San Pablo.

Two power outages in Alameda. At 2035PST winds knocked out power to around 3400 households and businesses. Gusty winds shook a branch loose from a tree near the intersection of Encinal Avenue and Walnut Street. The branch became entangled in the power lines, causing the outage. Power was restored at 2057PST. ||A second outage occurred at 2230PST affecting 100 households and businesses. Power was restored at 2350PST.

Strong winds gusting to up to 70 mph felled trees and power lines in both Scotts Valley and the San Lorenzo Valley. Electricity was cut to Scotts Valley and resulted in several small fires. 25,000 homes and businesses were without power. Damage included a large tree that crushed the roof of a home on the 100 block of Baja Sol Drive in Scotts Valley and another tree that fell on a home on the 400 block of Lockwood Lane. Trees also took down a transmission line.
Wind-whipped fire moved across a nursery in the Pajaro Valley burning a minivan and a large storage trailer.
Several large trees fell during the strong winds in the Half Moon Bay area.

High winds were blamed for speeding a fire that destroyed two homes and damaged a third in North Livermore near May Nissen Park. Even though the fire's cause is under investigation high winds had a significant effect on this event.
Power outages were caused by fallen trees in Oakland. Also, a Spruce tree fell onto the BART tracks in Hayward causing delays.

Wind has been blamed for spreading a fire that damaged 10 condominium units in the Walnut Creek area (200 block of County Brook Loop near Alcosta Blvd). Four other two bedroom condos had less serious damage. One resident was injured when they jumped out of their burning condo to the ground. The cause of the fire is unknown, but wind played a large part in spreading the fire.

A wind-driven fire destroyed a large barn in Santa Rosa and spread to two sheds and destroyed several vehicles. The fire also destroyed motorcycles, pickups, a riding lawn mower, and an RV. The fire was sparked by power lines that were blown to the ground.

At approximately 0647 PST State Route 152 was closed at the Santa Cruz/Santa Clara County line due to downed power lines. At approximately 0715 PST State Route 35 was closed 7.7 miles north of the junction of SR 17 due to downed trees.
Numerous road closures occurred in the Santa Cruz Mountains due to numerous trees and power lines down.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: The Highland Peak RAWS, located at 2,490 feet, reported a peak wind gusts of 75 mph at 0020 PST.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: The Los Vaqueros RAWS, located at 1,100 feet, reported a peak wind gusts of 60 mph at 1245 PST.
At approximately 0303 PST, the northbound SR 238 connector to northbound and southbound Interstate 880, in San Leandro, was closed due to a downed tree. The roadway reopened at 0440 PST.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: At approximately 0930 hours on January 22, 2012 State Route 1 was closed from 2 miles south of Lucia to 0.6 miles south of Lucia due to a slide. The roadway reopened to 1-way controlled traffic at 1308 hours on January 31, 2012.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: At approximately 2110 hours on January 19, 2012 State Route 1 was closed 5.5 miles north of Jenner due to a rock slide. The roadway reopened at 0200 hours on January 20, 2012.
A 58-foot sardine fishing boat (Stikine) sank about 2 miles off Pleasure Point early Friday morning in rough seas. Seas were reported up to 11 feet.

A roadway collapsed and slid to a street below in the Oakland Hills Saturday morning. Firefighters responding to an 8:55 am call found about 50 feet of road gone at the intersection of Oakwood Drive and Wild Currant Way.

In downtown Windsor residenta of four rental homes off Wild Oak Drive were awakened by a large oak tree that snapped at its base and crashed across the driveway, smashing at least one car and damaging the rooftop and gutter of one of the houses.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / HOLLISTER VALLEY / CARMEL VALLEY
events.event_narrative: Two large trees fell on the 1100 block of Wilma Drive and the 600 block of Seventh Street in Hollister. The tree that fell at the 600 block of Seventh Street knocked down power lines.
A large dead tree fell at a residence on Robin Drive and Arnold Drive in El Verano.

events.cz_name: SANTA CLARA VALLEY INCLUDING SAN JOSE
events.event_narrative: The Santa Clara County Sheriff's Department responded to four reports of downed trees, including Hecker Pass Highway at Rancho Vista Drive and along Santa Teresa Boulevard near Gavilan College.

In Santa Cruz strong winds caused at least two boats to break free from where they were anchored at the wharf, according to the harbor patrol. One boat washed ashore at Main Beach, sustaining severe damage.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Trees brought down a power line near Eighth Street and Park Avenue in Monterey.
More than 4000 Marin homes lost power due to strong winds.
Dense fog is blamed in 11 crashes on Highway 37 near Skaggs Island Rd. There were 31 vehicles involved in the crashes. Two people suffered minor injuries.
A man who was fishing Friday morning at Rio Del Mar Beach was carried out to sea by a Rip Current. The man was taken to a hospital where he was pronounced dead.

A fatal accident on the southbound lanes on SR 17 at Laurel Curve due to heavy rain. A 57 year old man lost control of his Nissan Sentra which slid from the southbound lanes into northbound traffic at 10:45 am. The Nissan struck a Chevy Suburban, spun around backward and bashed into a Toyota 4Runner which then collided with an Acura.
There were 39 traffic collisions in Santa Cruz County on Thursday due to heavy rain. Twentyone of the accidents occurred on Highway 17.
A fatal traffic accident as a 21 year old male died in a solo crash into a tree on Graham Hill Road early in the morning.
A 35 year old man crashed his Volkswagon Touareg on the onramp to southbound Highway 1 at State Park Drive about 12:45 am.

Strong gusty winds downed power lines in Santa Cruz County. In addition, a 40 foot catamaran moored near the Santa Cruz Municipal Wharf broke free in the afternoon and washed on to Seabright State Beach. No fuel was spilled.

In the Oakland Hills at At 4:21 am a tree fell onto the southbound lanes on SR 13 south of the Park Blvd off-ramp. A Toyota Camry carrying four people hit the tree and stopped in the center median. a Ford F-150 pickup then struck the tree and went airborne, hitting and killing the 18 year old driver of the Toyota Camry. The driver of the Ford Pickup and the three other passengers of the Toyota suffered non life threatening injuries.
Heavy rain brought the San Lorenzo River close to the Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk. Rushing water ripped apart a wooden staircase that goes down to the beach.
Two Monte Rio homes damaged by a large fallen tree at 8:59 pm. The tree, near a house on Starrett Hill Drive, became uprooted and fell across the road crashing into two houses on Moscow Road.
Motorists were involved in six rain-related accidents in Napa Valley.
Strong winds damaged the guest dock at the Martinez Marina. Three boats became unthethered.

Two accidents shut down Highway 1 for brief periods. One occurred on March 14 which was a head-on crash just south of Devil's Slide. Two sedans were involved with minor injuries to the two drivers. The other occurred on March 16 when two trucks collided at 10:45 am west of the turnoff for Ox Mountain landfill. Three riders suffered minor cuts and bruises.

On Wednesday night, Highway 9 near Celia Avenue was closed for at least an hour after a tree and power line fell into the road.||A mudslide closed Empire Grade Road about 4:30 pm Thursday. One lane was opened Thursday night.
A tree fell from the Woodbridge Village apartments on Hunt Avenue in Saint Helena onto a nearby house Wednesday night.
Two cars collided on westbound I-580 near Benedict Drive in San Leandro.

A series of accidents occurred. A driver went off the roadway on eastbound SR 24 near Wilder Rd in Orinda; a car spun out of control on eastbound I-80 near Willow Avenue in Hercules; and a pair of multicar crashes were reported on SR 24 and I-680 near Walnut Creek.
A large pine tree covers Montecito Avenue at Zieber Road in Santa Rosa.
A landslide closed Old Monte Rio Road between Sunny Drive and Cnopius Road.
A 50 foot oak tree landed on a Fitch Mountain Court home at 3:30 pm in Healdsburg.
A very large fir tree cleaved one Camp Meeker house in half and crushed another around 10:00 am. Camp Meeker is between Occidental and Monte Rio.
A tree fell across power lines on Mark West Springs Road north of Santa Rosa. A wire also fell in Guerneville.

At approximately 1546 hours SR 9 was closed 2.4 miles south of the North Junction of SR 236 due to a downed tree. At approximately 1554 hours, both lanes of SR 9 at McGaffin Mill Road were closed due to downed power lines.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: At approximately 0915 hours SR 1 was closed from 0.6 miles south of Stewarts Point to Stewarts Point due to a downed tree.
At approximately 2223 hours SR 13 was closed at Park Blvd, in Oakland due to a downed tree.
At approximately 0615 hours SR 9 was closed from 0.8 miles south of Felton to 0.4 miles south of Felton due to a downed tree.
A very large oak tree crushed portions of a three bedroom, two bath home on Cascade Drive in Fairfax around 7:00 pm.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / HOLLISTER VALLEY / CARMEL VALLEY
events.event_narrative: A farm worker picking crops in the fields near Salinas, California died as a result of excessive heat and heat stroke which lead to his having a heart attack.

At 3:40 PM an employee of the Santa Clara County OES observed a severe thunderstorm that produced large hail at his home. He measured hail from dime to quarter size that produced minor damage to plants around his home.

Spotters from the town of Gilroy in Santa Clara County reported that pea sized hail fell during a severe thunderstorm in the area. Hail accumulated up to depths of 2 inches across the area. Minor damage to vegetable plants was observed.

A man drowned in the waters of Soquel Creek in Capitola during a heavy rainstorm that produced minor flooding of the creek. He drowned in a section of the creek in Perry Park at the rear of a grocery store on 809 Bay Avenue in Capitola.

City of Petaluma flood monitoring gauges on Willow Brook at Penngrove Park measured at 62.0 feet. At 60.7 feet, water goes out of the banks.  Minor flooding in Petaluma in park lands along the brook and the Petaluma River.

City of Petaluma flood monitoring gauges on Willow Brook at Penngrove Park measured stage of 62.4 feet. At 60.7 feet water comes out of the banks. Minor flooding in Petaluma is observed in park land on Willow Brook and Petaluma River.

A CoCoRaHS spotter reports 3.50 inches of rain since 700 AM PST with a storm total of 4.88 inches. The spotter observed overwhelmed drainage culverts along the road that were backing up with significant erosion being reported.

CoCoRaHS spotter reports that rain intensity has increased and the flash flooding is beginning again with overwhelmed drainage culverts and flooding on the roadways with erosion of the banks around culverts observed.
Observations at Conn Dam measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Napa County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Sonoma County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 2020 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Santa Clara County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 479 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Santa Cruz County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 3288 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Monterey County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 1715 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Napa County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 3288 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Monterey County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 3368 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Monterey County due to the heavy rainfall.
Observations at 3400 feet elevation measured heavy rainfall. Minor urban and small stream flooding was observed across Santa Clara County due to the heavy rainfall.
Heavy rainfall measured at Conn Dam. Minor flooding of urban areas and small streams was observed across Napa County during this event.

Storm total rainfall of 8.03 inches measured at Mining Ridge RAWS site at 3288 feet elevation. 3.42 inches of this rain fell in the past 3 hours prior to the report. Minor flooding of urban areas and small streams was observed across Monterey County during this event.
Heavy rainfall measured at 479 feet elevation. Minor flooding of urban areas and small streams was observed across Santa Cruz County during this event.

Heavy rain led to two small sewage spills into creeks in the Ross Valley. More than 3,000 gallons spilled into the Sleepy Hollow Creek near Willow Way in San Anselmo. 1,000 gallons of sewage spilled into Fairfax Creek on Steven Court in Fairfax.
A pair of acacia trees was toppled by wind gusts estimated at 55 MPH. The trees blocked Carbonera drive in the Pasatiempo area. The trees also buried an SUV parked at the curb on the street.
Pacific Gas and Electric had 1300 customers reported without power in Santa Cruz County due to outages caused by wind gusts and fallen trees.
The general manager of pajaro dunes south said that 6 inches of water was covering beach road near shell drive due to heavy rainfall.
A large tree was blown down by strong wind gusts in the Pacific Heights neighborhood. Traffic was blocked for hours as a busy intersection was blocked and a car was smashed.
Following heavy rain on November 30, a mudslide shut down portions of Highway 84, Niles Canyon Road, to the east of Fremont. The California Highway Patrol closed the road due to the mudslide.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 56 MPH was measured at Pt. Reyes on the coast. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.
A wind gust of 61 MPH was measured at Spring Valley RAWS at elevation 1075 feet. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 60 MPH was measured at Rose Peak at elevation 3030 feet. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.
A wind gust of 75 MPH was measured at Los Gatos RAWS at elevation 1842 feet. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 56 MPH was measured at Highland Peak RAWS at elevation 2490 feet. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 62 MPH was measured at the coast. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 63 MPH was measured at Mill Valley at elevation 316 feet. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.
A wind gust of 63 MPH was measured at Spring Valley RAWS at elevation 1075 feet. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.
A wind gust of 84 MPH was measured at Los Gatos RAWS at 1842 feet elevation. Numerous trees down and some power outages occurred due to the wind gusts.
High winds brought down a tree on Old La Honda Road in Woodside that closed both lanes of traffic for several hours.
Downed power lines closed Trout Gulch Road and highland Way, and Highway 9 between Felton and Ben Lomond. Highway 9 was closed all day for Electric Company power line repairs.
Highway 84 was flooded between Decoto Road and Newark Boulevard and between Mission Boulevard and Main Street.
Alpine Road in San Mateo County was closed until noon due to downed trees and power lines.
High winds knocked trees down onto power lines which sparked a fire that burned down a small cabin near Fairfax, killing a person inside.
Hopper Creek flooded residential streets beginning around 5 AM with the water subsiding after the rains ended later Friday morning.
Caltrans reported southbound highway 29 was closed north of Peterson Drive near Bothe-Napa Valley State Park because of downed trees between 3 A.M. and 9:40 A.M. Friday.

EF-0 tornado moved onshore from Monterey Bay into coastal Santa Cruz County in the early morning of December 22. The tornado caused tree damage and significant damage to commercial greenhouse structures at a large farm. Broken fiberglass panels and bent metal frame poles were observed at the greenhouse with debris thrown several dozen yards south of the damage path into adjacent fields. the tornado caused additional minor damage to 4 adjacent greenhouse structures. Debris was wrapped around electric poles south of the damage path. The greenhouse operators indicated that they lost 25 percent of their lisianthus flower crop, over 3,000 Gerbea crop, and 40,000 square feet of greenhouse space. Minor tree damage was observed along San Andreas Road nearby. Damage path was 1.07 miles and 20 yards wide. Damage consistent with an EF-0 tornado estimated at 75 MPH.

Willow Brook at Penngrove Park gauge reached 62.1 feet. At a level of 60.7 feet, water from the Brook goes out of the banks and flooding begins in Penngrove Park. Above 62.0 feet, Willow Brook will flood downstream of Penngrove Park as well.
Stream Gauge on Soquel Creek reported water levels on the creek had risen to 14.62 feet. Flooding on the Creek begins above 14.5 feet.
The gauge on Willow Brook at Penngrove Park reached a level of 61.6 feet. Flooding begins in Penngrove Park with water going out of its banks and flooding the park at 60.7 feet.
The Big Trees gauge on the San Lorenzo River reached a level of 17.55 feet. Minor flooding in the area begins with levels above 17.0 feet at this location.
The Big Trees gauge on the San Lorenzo River reached 20.41 feet. Flooding on the river at this locations begins with levels above 17.0 feet.
Levels at the gauge on Pescadero Creek near Pescadero reached 12.86 feet. Minor flooding on the Creek at this location will begin with levels above 12.0 feet.
Soquel Creek stream gauge near Soquel reported a water level of 15.04 feet. In this area, Flooding begins at 14.5 feet. This is the peak value of the flash flooding event.
The gauge on Willow Brook at Penngrove Park reached a level of 60.9 feet. Flooding begins in Penngrove Park with water going out of its banks and flooding the park at 60.7 feet.
The water level on Corralitos Creek gauge at Freedom reached 11.61 feet. At this location, minor flooding begins above 11.5 feet.
The water level on the San Lorenzo River at the Big Trees Gauge reached 18.65 feet. Minor flooding begins at this location at levels above 17.0 feet.
The water level on the Pescadero Creek at Pescadero gauge reached 14.56 feet. Flooding begins at this location at levels above 12.0 feet. This is the peak level of the flash flood event.
The water level on the Pescadero Creek at Pescadero gauge reached 14.47 feet. Minor flooding begins at levels above 12.0 feet at this location.
The water levels on the Corralitos Creek at Freedom gauge reached 12.45 feet. Flooding begins at levels of 12.0 feet at this location.
The water level on the Pescadero Creek at Pescadero gauge reached 13.23 feet. At this location, flooding occurs with levels above 12.0 feet.

Water level reached 12.59 feet on San Anselmo Creek gauge. Gauge operators indicated that flooding begins above 11.1 feet on that gauge. Flooding was reported on nearby Sleepy Hollow Creek impacting lower floors of residences on Butterfield Road.
The water level on Willow Brook at Penngrove park reached 61.9 feet. Water on the creek at this location goes out of its banks at 60.7 feet with minor flooding in Penngrove Park in Petaluma.
The water level on Willow Brook at Penngrove park reached 62.1 feet. Water on the creek at this location goes out of its banks at 60.7 feet with minor flooding in Penngrove Park in Petaluma.
The water level on the Big Sur River near Big Sur reached 10.42 feet. Flooding begins with levels above 10.0 feet with minor flash flooding in the Big Sur area.
Law Enforcement reported Roadway Flooding along Carriage Lane.
Law enforcement reports minor flooding of roadways.
Law Enforcement reports Highway flooding along Highway 37.
Law enforcement reports roadway flooding on U.S. Highway 101 near San Antonio Road.
Flooding of several roadways in the area reported by law enforcement.
Minor Flooding on Willow Brook observed.
Law enforcement reports flooding on U.S. Highway 101.
Law enforcement reports street flooding on 8th street.
Law enforcement reported roadway flooding on Interstate 680 N at Sycamore Valley Road.
Law Enforcement reports flooding leading to road closures at the intersection of Green Valley Road and State Route 116.
Road washed out at Vine Hill Road near Highway 17 due to flooding.
The Church Street Muni station was shut down due to flooding, which resulted in a loss of service on the line from West Portal to the Embarcadero.

Numerous trees down across the City of San Francisco. Newspaper reports that public works responded to over 40 downed trees. Blocked roadways at California and Cherry Streets in Laurel Heights were reported. Washington Square, Mount Davidson, and Golden Gate parks reported trees down. Several roads were closed in Golden Gate Park including MLK Drive, 25th Avenue, and 47th Avenue between Fulton Street and JFK Drive. 10 cars were damaged by falling tree branches.

Power lines were blown down across Smith Ranch Road in San Rafael. Two power poles were snapped off on highway 101 in Terra Linda, closing the northbound offramp to Lucas Valley-Smith Ranch Road. Power lines fell at the Park n Ride lot and across Redwood Boulevard. Smith Ranch Road was closed between Redwood and the Freeway and a stretch of Redwood Boulevard was closed south of Paul Drive.

Strong winds blew a big rig that was eastbound on the Richmond-San Rafael Bridge onto its side. Eastbound lanes of the bridge were blocked for more than five hours with traffic reduced to using a shoulder to pass. Winds continued to be strong through the morning, and crews could not remove the vehicle due to the wind speeds on the bridge. The truck was removed by crews around 10 AM that morning.

Flooding damaged White Hill Middle School and classes were cancelled on Monday December 3rd due to classrooms being flooded. Significant flooding occurred with the library and several other classrooms covered in mud. Two art classrooms and two seventh grade classrooms, as well as an administrative office and a staff room suffered water damage.

High wind felled several trees in Napa County. A large oak tree branch punctured the roof of a home on Lake Street in Napa County. A 40 foot fir tree on Cedar Street fell due to high winds and took out a water tank, fencing, and part of a roof and back porch.
A pair of businesses were damaged in Windsor at 239 Windsor River Road. The top of a pine tree was blown off by strong winds, and pierece the roof of the businesses.
High winds brought down a power pole and trees in Schellville on Broadway, south of Watermaugh. Broadway was closed for several hours.
Heavy rain flooded the intersection of Highways 12 and 121 in Schellville for about 45 minutes. Traffic was blocked and could not cross the intersection during this time.

California Highway Patrol reported a two car accident during heavy rainfall in Napa County. At 2:25 PM on Saturday the 22nd of December, a car heading southbound on Highway 121 near the Viansa winery lost control on a curve, crossed the center line and was hit broadside by oncoming traffic. The driver was killed at the scene and the passenger sustained significant injuries and was airlifted. The driver of the car in oncoming traffic was also airlifted with significant injuries.

More than 100 flights were cancelled in and out of San Francisco International Airport (KSFO) due to the heavy rain and low clouds on one of the busiest travel days of the year. Passengers were delayed for an average of 3 hours because two runways were shut down.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Minor coastal flooding in Marin County at the time of the King Tide caused Highway 1 to be closed at the time of high tide.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Streets in Mill Valley were flooded at the time of high tide during the King Tide.
Heavy rain caused a mudslide which blocked the southbound lanes of Felton Empire Road, near Bonny Doon.
Lincoln Street in Watsonville was closed after high winds blew a tree down onto powerlines, all of which fell into the road.
Highway 9 was closed near El Solyo Heights Drive in Felton due to wires falling across the road.
A large tree fell onto the roof of a vacant house in Sebastopol on Robinson Road. The tree fell between the garage and the home next door, taking down a deck and a chimney.
High winds cause a power pole to fall at Hall Road and Third Street in Sebastopol. It took down a high voltage line and cut power to a significant portion of western Santa Rosa.
High winds blew down a massive redwood tree onto a car in Santa Rosa.
Hopper Creek rose to the top of the bridge on Finnell Road, overflowed down Mulberry Street, and flooded the south end of Heather Street.

Washington Street was flooded on both sides of its intersection with California Drive for several hours early in the afternoon of December 23. The Napa Valley Wine train shortened its route due to water on the tracks.
Cal Fire reported a tree fell onto a house in Bonny Doon on Northwest Drive. No injuries ocurred.
Wires were downed due to high winds in Corralitos. Eureka Canyon Road near Old Evans Road was closed around 10 PM.
A 30 foot tree fell on Ice Cream Grade, near Winter Creek Road with no major damage and no injuries.

Highland Way in the Santa Cruz Mountains was blocked by a mudlside. The road was initially flooded due to heavy rain and then a mudslide ocurred shortly after. The slide blocked all traffic and closed the road. Public works estimated the road will be closed for one week.

A massive rock and mud slide near Partinigton Creek blocked US Highway 1 and a private road leading into a Partington Ridge neighborhood. 32 homes were isolated due to the rocks and mud blocking the roadway. Highway 1 was closed for 5 days due to the slide until one lane could be opened again. More than 40 stranded tourists slept in their cars Saturday night December 22nd as they had no way to get out of the area. Repairs took several weeks.

Evacuations to 50 homes in Felton on Sunday night. The San Lorenzo River flooded several streets, including Sylvan Way, River Road, Covered Bridge Road and Circle Road. Residents were able to return home around 11:00 PM that night.

During vigorous rain, Stony Point Road had to be closed in Coati. A 48 inch culvert underneath the road collapsed and left behind a 10 foot hole in the middle of Stony Point Road, in front of the Sports City Indoor Complex. Engineers planned emergency repairs to reopen the road by the end of the next day.
Mudslides closed Annapolis Road for several hours, east of Highway 1.
Downed power lines and a fallen tree closed Highway 12 near Watmaugh Road, south of Sonoma, for several hours on Sunday afternoon, December 23.
A van full of people stalled in knee-deep water from Atascadero Creek on Graton Road. The people were stranded for 20 minutes before being rescued by fire crews.
Two motorists had to be rescued from waist deep water on Highway 1 where Walker Creek flooded the roadway near Tomales. The road was then closed due to high water.
Wind blew down a large pine tree, which crashed into a playground structure in Corte Madera's Town Park on Sunday morning.

Heavy rain caused San Francisquito Creek to flood and briefly overtop a levee in East Palo Alto. Numerous other seeps and areas where water bubbled through the levee were also noted in the area. Homes on Verbena Drive nearest the levee were evacuated. Officials placed sandbags on top of the levees to temporarily strengthen the flood defenses.

During heavy rainfall, a 24 inch culvert failed and collapsed, opening up a 20 foot sinkhole on Tarabrook Drive. One lane of traffic could still get by the sinkhole. The Orinda City Council declared a state of emergency due to this large sinkhole.
Sonoma County officials reported that an oak tree fell and blocked Bennett Valley Road near Lafranconi Road at 7:10 A.M. on Wednesday morning. The tree was struck by a car. There were no injuries.
Highway 1 was closed north of Jenner due to a significant mud and rock slide blocking the lanes of the road.
Heavy rains produced flooding of the Ross Valley Sanitary District sewer system. A massive sewage spill ocurred in San Anselmo where 30,000 gallons of sewage spilled into Sleepy Hollow Creek.
Heavy rain triggered a mud and landslide that lead to a washout of Vine Hill Road. The road was completely closed for 4 days for repairs.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A pair of fishermen, father and son, and a friend were fishing on rocks near the Golden Gate Bridge. A large sneaker wave swept them off the rocks and into the ocean. The friend was able to swim back to shore and contacted authorities. A Tiburon Fire Department boat found the bodies of the father and son about 100 yards offshore with the assistance of a Coast Guard Helicopter.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A visitor to Point Reyes was walking along the beach with his wife and their dog. A wave swept their dog into the ocean, and the man and his wife went into the water after their dog. The wife and dog made it out of the water, but the man did not and was carried out to sea. A coast guard helicopter and life boat found the man's body later that afternoon and he was pronounced dead.
During a cold snap, a man brought a charcoal barbecue grill into his house to keep warm. The man died due to carbon monoxide poisoning and his roommate was taken to the hospital for treatment.
In Petaluma, a man sought shelter inside of a dumpster trash bin during sub-freezing temperatures to stay warm. He died when a trash truck picked up the dumpster and compacted the contents.
High winds blew down 10 inch diameter tree branches which blocked the westbound lane of Bear Creek Road.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Strong winds blew down trees and power lines across Mission Road near Monterey.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: NPS observation of winds at Point Sur Light Station of 65 MPH.
Strong winds blew down a tree, blocking a roadway near Inverness.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / HOLLISTER VALLEY / CARMEL VALLEY
events.event_narrative: Strong winds blew down a eucalyptus tree, blocking the northbound lane of River Road about 10 miles SE of Salinas.
Strong winds blew down a tree on an overhead utility pole, six miles NE of Daly City.
Strong winds blew power lines and a pole down in the roadway with a tree across the roadway, near the intersection of Pine Flat and Ice Cream Grade Roads about 4 miles NW of Felton.
Strong winds blew a tree down and blocked southbound Highway 101, just south of the Golden Gate Bridge.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS OF SAN BENITO COUNTY AND INTERIOR MONTEREY COUNTY INCLUDING PINNACLES NATIONAL MONUMENT
events.event_narrative: The Santa Rita RAWS in San Benito County measured a peak wind gust of 60 MPH.
Strong wind blew down small tree branches and debris onto streets in the city of Petaluma.
Strong winds blew down a large tree branch, blocking the middle of the lane at State Road 116 and F Street near Monte Rio.
High winds blew out the front window of a house in Daly City with glass everywhere.
High winds impacted operations at San Francisco International Airport overnight with wind gusts measured at 60 MPH.
High winds measured on the Woodacre RAWS with a gust of 59 MPH.
High winds were observed, with a 62 MPH wind gust measured bv a home weather station near Ocean Beach.
High winds observed with a measured wind gust of 62 MPH at Fort Funston.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: High winds were measured with a 61 MPH gust at the GOES Station PEAC1 about 9 miles ENE of Fremont.

High winds which gusted over 60 MPH across San Francisco and the surrounding areas produced thousands of power outages. Newspaper accounts show at least 17,000 customers out of power in various locations around the Bay Area on April 8. This included nearly 5,000 customers in the city of San Francisco itself.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind gusts tore off part of a roof of a small building at Masons Marina on Westshore Road at Bodega Bay. The roof fell onto a propane tank which broke a valve on the tanks and caused a gas leak.
Strong winds blew down power lines, blocking highway 84 about 3 miles south of Woodside.

events.cz_name: SAN FRANCISCO / SAN PABLO / SUISUN BAY AND W DELTA
events.event_narrative: Southwest winds caused a 72 foot long America's Cup Yacht to capsize during training runs in San Francisco Bay. 12 people were onboard the yacht when it capsized and had to be rescued. There was one fatality.

Strong winds knocked down power lines in the hills of Napa County which started several wildfires. This included a 75 acre fire near Yountville that destroyed a barn and a 20 acre fire near Soda Springs that burned a historic slaughterhouse on a ranch. A larger fire, known as the Yellow Fire, burned near Knights Valley in Sonoma County and consumed over 125 acres.

Near Angwin, strong winds caused a tree branch to fall that struck a power line and started a fire. The fire burned the tree and the roof of a 5000 square foot barn. The fire burned half an acre and damaged the barn.
Strong winds caused a 65 foot high oak tree to fall on power lines which started a half acre fire in the nearby grass and brush.
A wind gust was measured at the Hawkeye RAWS, elevation 2024 feet, of 56 MPH. Trees and powerlines were downed in the area with several fires started as a result.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Mt. Diablo RAWS measured a wind gust of 71 MPH at elevation 3849 feet.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: A large fire in the Stony Valley section of Ft. Hunter Liggett burned about 600 acres before being contained by base fire personnel. The blaze resulted in intermittent closures of Nacimiento-Fergusson Road.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Observations from the Lick Observatory on Mt. Hamilton at elevation around 4000 feet, measured a wind gust of 64 MPH.

Four people were swept into the ocean by a sneaker wave at Bonny Doon Beach in Santa Cruz County. Two of the men reached nearby rocks and were rescued by a Coast Guard helicopter. The two women died as a result of drowning.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: The Mission Wildfire broke out on Fort Hunter Liggett on August 22 and quickly grew to consume 4500 acres. One private home was threatened but not destroyed. The fire was contained on August 26.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Measured 57 MPH gust at Los Vaqueros RAWS at elevation 1100 feet.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Fences were knocked down due to strong winds in Oakland along Monterey Boulevard. A large tree was knocked down at Skyline and Redwood Roads. Wind gusts were measured at 54 MPH at the Oakland North RAWS at this time. The RAWS is located at 1400 feet elevation.
A tree was downed due to strong winds outside Alamo in the community of Diablo. The downed tree blocked the road into the Diablo Country Club neighborhood.
In San Leandro, a huge tree was downed due to strong winds on Halceon Avenue.
In Napa, strong winds caused a tree to fall on a pickup truck. It happened in the area of Solano and Oak Knoll Avenues. The tree shattered the windshield and the branches went into the truck.
During the event, power outages impacted up to 2000 customers in the San Francisco Metro area.

Downed power lines ignited a wild fire along Berryessa Knoxville Road in Napa County on the north side of Lake Berryessa. The fire spread quickly due to 40-50 MPH wind and consumed over 400 acres but was contained by early afternoon. No structures were damaged or destroyed.
