Strong winds in San Francisco knocked over two stories of scaffolding at a building under renovation at 20th and Deharo Streets. The scaffolding fell into a set of power lines.
A large tree was blown over and blocked 3 of the 4 lanes of traffic on Masonic Avenue and Fell Street early Friday morning.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: Wind gusts of 75 MPH measured on a mesonet site in Altamont Pass. Tractor trailers were blown over on the highway through Altamont Pass.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS OF SAN BENITO COUNTY AND INTERIOR MONTEREY COUNTY INCLUDING PINNACLES NATIONAL PARK
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 69 MPH was measured at the Santa Rita Mesonet Site in San Benito County at an elevation of 5000 feet.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 62 MPH was measured on the Los Vaqueros RAWS at elevation 1100 feet.

events.cz_name: EAST BAY HILLS AND THE DIABLO RANGE
events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 61 MPH was measured on the Calaveras Road RAWS at elevation 1230 feet.
Strong winds blew a tree down on a house in Antioch. The tree branches broke through the roof and into a bedroom where it injured a man by cutting his back.
Strong winds knocked down scaffolding and metal awnings at the Bay Street Shopping Center in Emeryville.
Strong Winds blew a large tree branch down onto a fence and into the backyard of a house in Redwood City.
Strong winds resulted in power outages to 3200 customers in Antioch.
Public works department in San Francisco responded to three calls for downed trees due to high wind at Van Ness Avenue and Pine Street, Valencia and 20th Street, and Third and 20th Street.

Wind blew down a tree which blocked all northbound lanes of Interstate 238 on the edge of San Leandro and fell on a car. Several cars then struck the downed tree before the highway was closed for one hour.
Wind blew down a large tree onto a van on 4th street in Santa Rosa.
Winds knocked down power lines and produced outages to 28,600 homes across Sonoma County at the peak of the event.
Winds blew down a tree in the Rockbridge area of Oakland along Keith Avenue near the Broadway exit to highway 24. Power lines came down with the tree.
A tree was felled by strong winds onto a car driving on US Highway 101 in Petaluma. The occupant of the car was injured.
Wind blowing down powerlines started the silverado fire near the intersection of Silverado Trail and Soda Canyon Road north of Napa. Approximately 300 acres were consumed with mandatory evacuations.
A tree branch was knocked down by strong winds in the 2000 block of Austin Street in the Fruitvale District of Oakland. The branch fell on a man on the street and killed him.
A tree fell into the 13000 block of Skyline Boulevard. A car on the street swerved to avoid the fallen tree, and crashed into another tree. The driver of the car was killed in the accident.
Strong winds blew down a cedar tree onto power lines on Blake Street in Berkeley, between Mathews and Mabel Streets.
Strong winds caused downed live wires near Bella Vista Elementary School located on 1025 E 28th Street in East Oakland.
Emeryville Police reported branches down from strong winds across the city. A car was damaged by a falling tree on the 4300 block of Adeline Street with no injuries.
Strong winds knocked down a very old Eucalyptus Tree by Lake Merritt. The tree was about 150 feet tall.
At the peak of the storms Thursday night and Friday morning, 42,500 customers in Berkeley and Oakland were without power due to downed trees and power lines.
The Oakland Fire Department reported 148 tree related calls and 81 calls of issues including downed wires and arcing. These were due to the strong winds.
Several fallen trees blocked the Northbound lanes of the 3600 block of Martin Luther King Jr. Way.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: The Pfeiffer Fire started on December 17th 2013 around midnight in the vicinity of Pfeiffer Ridge in the Monterey Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. The fire burned 917 acres. Thirty four (34) residence and 4 outbuildings were damaged/destroyed. The fire was declared contained on December 20 2013 at 6:00 p.m.

A man was boogie boarding in Monterey Bay near the Santa Cruz Lighthouse in very rough surf. Lifeguards approached him and attempted to remove him from the area but he did not want assistance. Shortly after, a set of waves slammed him into the rocks. Rescue swimmers went in and were unable to retrieve him due to rough surf - in fact they were injured themselves. A second set of swimmers were able to get the man, and pulled him from the water. He was taken to a local hospital but later died.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: A man was fishing in Point Reyes National Seashore near the lighthouse. A wave knocked over his ice cooler and carried it into the ocean. He went into the water to attempt to retrieve the cooler and was overcome by large waves.
Several inches of standing water covering all lanes near Interstate 280 and Highway 87.
Roadway flooding reported on Walters Road.
Roadway flooding reported on the US 101 and Portero Avenue On ramp at Cesar Chavez.
Flooding reported on the Interstate 280 Off Ramp at Saratoga.
Roadway flooding reported along the Great Highway between Lincoln and Sloat.
Roadway flooding reported on the Dunne Avenue On Ramp at Southbound US Highway 101 in Morgan Hill.
Flooding reported on Moffett Off Ramp on State Route 85 Northbound.

Firefighters rescued a homeless man from the waters of Coyote Creek near the San Jose Municipal Golf Course. He was stuck in waist deep water, clinging to trees and debris. He was taken to the hospital to be treated for fatigue and hypothermia.
Report of standing water covering the Shoreline Boulevard on ramp at US 101 Northbound.
Standing water, six inches deep, was reported covering the roadways at US Highway 101 and Interstate 280.
Roadway flooding reported over both lanes of State Road 152 between Canada and Ferguson.
Flooding reported on the Cochrane Road Onramp to Southbound US Highway 101.
Flooding reported on San Tomas Expressway at Pruneridge Avenue in the slow lane.
Flooding reported at the intersection of San Martin Avenue and Monterey Highway in Gilroy.
Flooding reported on Northbound US Highway 101 at Bernal.
Flooding reported in the left turn lane on Southbound US Highway 101 at San Antonio Road.
Flooding reported across all lanes on Tomales Road at Valley Ford Road.
Measured 64 MPH wind gust at the Los Gatos RAWS site, elevation 1842 feet.
Rock and mudslide blocking portions of Highway 1 at Panoramic.
Active slide reported from the Pfieffer Burn Scar at Sycamore Canyon Road.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Power Lines reported downed by winds on San Remo Road.
Mudslide reported on Priest Valley Road.
Small mudslide reported on Highway 1 Northbound near Garrapatta State Park.
Tree down across both lanes of Jarvis Road.
Tree down due to winds, blocking the intersection of Knightsen Avenue and Delta Road.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY / HOLLISTER VALLEY / CARMEL VALLEY
events.event_narrative: A 25 foot tree downed by wind, blocking both lanes of Larkspur Court.
A 30 foot tree downed by winds at Lincoln Way and 37th Avenue, 6 miles NW of Daly City in San Francisco County.

events.cz_name: MOUNTAINS OF SAN BENITO COUNTY AND INTERIOR MONTEREY COUNTY INCLUDING PINNACLES NATIONAL PARK
events.event_narrative: Measured gust of 59 MPH at the Santa Rita RAWS at elevation 5000 feet.

events.cz_name: SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST
events.event_narrative: A gust of 71 MPH was measured at the Highlands Peak Mesonet site, elevation 2490 feet.
Utility company reporting that 2500 customers are without power in Napa at this time.
Traffic hazard due to downed tree and power lines near Bonny Dune Road and Smith Grade.
Flooded streets reported around the 2 AM Club.
Flooding closed State Route 121 at Highway 12 near Sonoma.
Spotter reported this as a 24 Hour Rainfall Total.
Spotter reported this as a 24 hour rainfall total.
Rainfall total reported since 10 AM yesterday with an additional 0.54 inches of rainfall since 10 AM today.
Spotter reported this as a 24 hour rainfall total.
Spotter reported this as a 24 hour rainfall total.
SUV stuck in standing water, reported to be halfway up the door.
Vehicle stuck in mud and water, party had to be rescued as they were unable to exit the vehicle.
A teenager at Panther Beach slipped from ocean rocks and was caught in the high surf. Rescuers were able to pull him from the water but were unable to revive him.

events.cz_name: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
events.event_narrative: Two men were fishing on rocks in the Marin Headlands. A sneaker wave swept them off the rocks south of Rodeo Beach and into the Ocean. The Coast Guard, National Park Service, and Southern Marin figherfighters responded. They found one individual clinging to rocks and rescued him and he was treated for hypothermia. One victim was found by a Coast Guard boat in the water, deceased.

Three people were on the beach at Gray Whale Cove when a Sneaker Wave washed them out into the ocean. A dozen beachgoers formed a human chain and pulled the three from the water. Emergency responders performed CPR on a woman pulled from the surf. She was airlifted to a hospital but died. The other two people rescued were treated for hypothermia.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Two beachgoers at Asilomar State Beach were swept into the water by a sneaker wave. A surfer was able to rescue one of the people but could not find the second person. The Coast Guard conducted an extensive search but was not able to locate the second person.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY AND BIG SUR COAST
events.event_narrative: Four people were fishing on rocks at Soberanes Point when a sneaker wave washed one of them out to sea. The Coast Guard and rescue crews attempted to rescue him but could not find him. His body was recovered by rescue divers the next day.

events.cz_name: POINT ARENA TO POINT REYES...OUT TO 10 NM
events.event_narrative: High surf and potentially a rouge wave occurred in Bodega Bay, capsizing a 32 foot long vessel after an early morning crabbing trip on the opening day of recreational crab season. Five people on the boat were thrown into the water, none of them were wearing life jackets. Four of the people died in the water and one was able to swim to shore and was rescued later by a helicopter crew. The incident was not directly caused by local wind conditions, but distant wind in a strong Pacific Storm created the swell conditions that caused this incident.
Rainfall accumulated in only 20 minutes. Lightning and thunder reported by observer.
Rainfall accumulated in 5 minutes. Lightning and thunder observed along with very small hail.

Hail of 1/2 inch diameter fell in downtown Napa and across the southern part of Napa County. Hail accumulated to a depth of 3 to 6 inches in some places and produced leaf damage to trees and plants in the city.

Gusty winds toppled a few trees in the Presidio of San Francisco and brought down powerlines. A large cypress tree fell and brought down adjacent power lines. Fallen live wires forced the closure of Infantry Terrace and Moraga Avenue.
A ficus tree was snapped by a wind gust. The tree fell on a taxi and broke the car's windshield. The driver was unhurt. Other parked cars nearby sustained minor damage.
Heavy rain produced flooding of the Interstate 580 onramp in Dublin. A car stalled in the flooded ramp.

Significant flash flooding on Interstate 280 was reported by the public. This coincided with a nearby observation of 0.90 of rainfall in 30 minutes at San Bruno Mountain. Traffic was significantly impacted and slowed or stopped during the height of morning rush hour.
California Highway Patrol observed 18 inches of water on roadway on WestBound Interstate 580 to Eastbound Route 24.
Flooding from Pt. Reyes to Olema on Highway 1. Campground flooded.
Public reports water covering roadway and parking lots along San Pedro Creek.
Flash flood swept SUV off road and into Dry Creek.
Northbound US-101 flooded across all lanes, north of Arata Lane.
Significant amount of water across area roadways near Laguna de Santa Rosa.
Flooding on all lanes of Northbound US-101 at Lucky Drive.
Foss Creek over banks and flooding Vine and Grove. Law enforcement closed roads.
Law enforcement reports numerous road closures due to flooding in Healdsburg. Intersections included Piper at East, Center at Grant, Piper at Healdsburg, and Center at Mitchell.
Standing water causing roadway flooding in Healdsburg.
Water flooding all lanes of Route 29 near Napa.
Roadway flooding at Mojo Cojo Slough on Moss Landing.
Roadway flooding on Southbound US-101 at 85.
CHP reports water 1 foot deep covering almost entire Parkmoor Onramp to Interstate 280 Soutbound.
Roadway flooding reported at intersection of Highway 1 and Struve Road.
Roadway flooding reported from intersection of Meridian Road and Archer Road.
Multiple lanes of CA-92 blocked due to flooding, west of Interstate 880.
Ashby Avenue Railway underpass near I-80 is flooded. Three cars are stranded and floating in floodwaters.
Parking lots of Elsie Allen High School flooded.
Highway 1 flooded and closed from Panoramic Highway to Muir Woods Road.
CA-121 flooded at Schellville due to Schell Creek.
The Russian River flooded and resulted in closure of CA-128 between Canyon Road and Alexander Valley Road including Geyserville.
Fifteen homes were flooded and damaged due to flooding from Santa Rita Creek along Russel Road in Salinas.
US-101 closed in both directions due to flooding in Menlo Park between Willow and Marsh exits.
Rainfall totals of 4.5 inches so far, with 2.5 inches since midnight.
Spotter measures rainfall total from 5:00 PM December 10  through 7:30 AM December 11 of 3.97 inches.
A large number of boats in Monterey Harbor had to be pumped out to avoid sinking on December 11 due to heavy rainfall.
Spotter has measured 4.19 inches of rainfall since midnight and a storm total of six inches so far.
The Venado gauge in Northern Sonoma County measured a 24 hour rainfall of 9 inches.
Heavy rainfall resulted in the partial roof collapse of a Grocery Store in San Jose.
Heavy rain overwhelmed the sewage plant in Castroville resulting in a sewage spill.

Heavy rain caused flooding of several trailer parks in Redwood City. The combination of standing water and a local creek flooding resulted in the need for residents to be evacuated from the Le Mar Trailer Park and RC Mobile Home Park on E Bayshore in Redwood City. 50 mobile homes were evacuated and residents were sent to shelters.

Heavy rainfall produced significant rises on Novato Creek between highways 101 and 37 on the east side of the city of Novato. This led to an intentional breach of the levee on a 20 foot section to prevent floodwaters from reaching downtown businesses and nearby subdivisions. This same flooding also resulted in failure of a smaller portion of the levee and overtopped another section. Caltrans levees on highway 37 were breached and a culvert was washed out.
A slide under sixty feet of Highway 1 near Muir Beach resulted in a full closure of the road which is expected to last for several months.
A significant mudslide occurred along Tennessee Valley Road.
Downed trees and power lines in San Francisco resulted in outages impacting up to 95,000 customers.
San Bruno BART station closed during rush hour commute due to flooding of station from heavy rain.
Elevated water levels, strong winds, and swell produced water that flooded over the wall on the Embarcadero and resulted in the road being closed for several hours.

Strong wind gusts blew down an 80 foot cypress tree at Gateway School in Santa Cruz into an area where children were congregating outside waiting for school to begin. At 8:50 AM PST on the morning of January 6, 2016, a weak tornado touched down in a field between Highway 156 and Orchard Road approximately 7 miles north of Hollister, CA in San Benito County. Results from a damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service later that day showed the damage to be consistent with a tornado	of EF-0 intensity (maximum wind speeds of 75 MPH). The tornado lasted just a minute or two and caused spotty damage along a 3/4-mile length path 10-20 yards in width that crossed Orchard Road as it moved to the north-northeast. A weak non-supercell EF0 tornado occurred Friday April 22, 2016 at around 4 pm associated with a line of showers along the leading edge of a cold front. Due to its non-supercell status, it will be referred to as a landspout, but is in the family of tornados.||Friday evening, 22 April, the Monterey WFO WCM was informed by a local TV meteorologist of a video posted to facebook showing a possible tornado or dust devil. The video was posted by and on the KRKC, Greenfield radio station, facebook page. Through the course of the evening of the 22nd and morning of the 23rd, the MTR WCM and WFO staff continued investigation through following up with the reporting TV meteorologist and reaching out to KRKC via facebook and email. By Saturday morning the 23rd the address and point of contact at the storm location was obtained and a storm survey was initiated.||The WFO MTR WCM was dispatched Saturday morning to perform a storm survey. The storm survey was done through the use of the Damage Assessment Toolkit (DAT) on the office iPad. Interviews were also conducted of eyewitnesses as part of the survey.|The visual survey was done with the help of an eyewitness who described where the landspout began, the path it took, damage it inflicted, and provided the visual confirmation of rotation. According to multiple accounts, the landspout began on the hillside NW of a small farm community, laying nearly flat a broad oak tree. As the landspout moved down the hill it likely went through a period of vortex stretching, allowing it to tighten up and spin a bit faster. Eyewitnesses say the landspout moved down off the hill and toward several small houses. It displaced two normal sized steel dumpsters about 30 yards in the direction of its travel. Along this flat land portion of the path the landspout encountered two oak trees, tearing off several large branches (3in diameter) and depositing them 20-30 yards away in a downpath direction. Damage assessment indicates the landspout weakened significantly while passing over several small housing structures and brushing by a barn. Once past these structures it encountered another downhill slope and re-intensified. The landspout then encountered a pole barn with a small to moderate size trailer parked beneath. There were no visible signs of damage to the trailer, but the pole barn showed significant roof damage. It is estimated that about half of the roof from the pole barn was damaged or torn off with this debris strewn about the area. Rotation is easily confirmed due to debris locations. Parts of the roof were thrown orthogonally to the right of the direction of movement, as far as 40 to 50 yards. Other portions of the roof were lifted up, taken with the landspout and scattered across a neighboring vineyard. The farthest deposit away from the pole barn is estimated at about 60 to 80 yards, along the landspout path to the southeast. Eyewitness video posted on KRKC facebook page shows the landspout at the far edge of the vineyard and entering a rapid dissipation phase.||Eyewitness accounts also included the following:.|No significant winds outside of the landspout.|Ears popping as the landspout passed.|A palette spinning in the air in the landspout���s early phase.|No palette was found and no damage from the palette was reported.|Thunder was heard in the area preceding the landspout.|Brief intense heavy rain followed the landspout.|One person reported two distinct circulations; one that descended from the cloud base and another that followed which spun up off the ground.||Atmospheric and observation conditions included:.|Occurred along the leading edge of a passing cold front.|Cloud bases were estimated from eyewitness video to be around 5kft.|Radar showed showers in the area.|Lowest angle of radar beam was at about 9-10kft over the area.|Appears to be a case of low topped convection which is normal for the immediate west coast.|Wind data in the area did not show significant speeds.

Waterspout formed on lake Berryessa during cold frontal passage. This was filmed by people visiting the lake and was only a blip on the radar due to distance and elevation from the radar. |LSR: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=LSRMTR&e=201604281650 .|Write up: http://www.wrh.noaa.gov/mtr/stormSummary/SvrWx4_27_16/svrwx_4_27_16.php .

Began to see reports via social media of localized, low level urban flooding due to heavy rain and hail, so we investigated. To attain some ground truth, WCM called petro facility that the convection crossed. He spoke with the plant supervisor who was from Texas and knows severe weather. The supervisor was able to provide photos and video of the hail falling and accumulating. He said at its peak, the hail had depths of about 3 inches, but just under dime size at most. The hail melted quickly and caused local ponding of water.||No impacts were reported.|See http://www.wrh.noaa.gov/mtr/stormSummary/SvrWx4_27_16/svrwx_4_27_16.php for pics and details.

Heavy rain caused the Alameda Creek to flood.  The stream gauge on Alameda Creek near Niles to rise above flood stage between 8:45 pm PST on January 10 and 5:30 am PST on January 11.

Heavy rain over the Soberanes Burn Scar resulted in flooding on the Big Sur River. The Big Sur River stream gauge near Big Sur rose above flood stage at 7:00 pm PST on January 10 and continued above flood stage until 6:30 am PST on January 11.

Heavy rain resulted in flooding on the Sonoma Creek.  The Sonoma Creek stream gauge at Agua Caliente rose above flood stage at 7:30 pm PST on January 18 and remained above flood stage until 10:30 pm PST.

Heavy rain on January 18 caused the Laguna de Santa Rosa to flood. The stream gauge on the Laguna de Santa Rosa at Stony Point Road rose above flood stage at 7:45 pm PST on January 18 and remained above flood stage until 1:45 am PST on January 19.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding on both the Willow Brook at Penngrove and Sonoma Creek at Agua Caliente.  The Sonoma Creek stream gauge at Agua Caliente rose above flood stage at 4:45 am on January 20 and remained above flood stage until 8 am that day.
Heavy rain caused the Napa River at Lodi Lane in Saint Helena CA to exceed flood stage between 3:00-10:30 pm PST on January 10, 2017.
Corte Madera Creek stream gauge at Ross exceeded flood stage between 6:43 pm and 8:00 pm PST on January 10.

Heavy rain in the Santa Cruz Mountains resulted in flooding on the San Lorenzo River.  The San Lorenzo stream gauge at Big Trees rose above flood stage at 7:25 am PST on January 20 and remained above flood stage until 8:30 am PST.
The Pacheco Creek near Dunneville flooded.  A stream gauge on the Pacheco Creek near Dunneville rose above flood stage at 10:30 AM PST and remained above flood stage until 4:15 PM PST.

Heavy rain on January 22, 2017, resulted in flooding on the Sonoma Creek.  The Sonoma Creek stream gauge at Agua Caliente rose above flood stage at 4:15 AM PST on January 22 and remained above flood stage until 8:30 AM PST.
Remote rain gauge data in the Loma Burn Scar indicated rain rates approaching 0.75 per hour, rates that were predetermined to cause debris flows in the burn scar.

Heavy rain on January 24 caused the Pacheco Creek in San Benito County to flood.  The Pacheco Creek stream gauge near Dunneville rose above flood stage at 11:45 am PST on January 22 and remained above flood stage until 4 pm PST on January 22.

Heavy rain in the Santa Cruz Mountains caused the San Lorenzo River to flood. The San Lorenzo River stream gauge at Big Trees exceeded flood stage between 8:45 pm on January 10 and 1:30 am on January 11.

On the morning of the 16th, lightning started multiple wildfires in Santa Cruz/San Mateo Counties that combined to form the CZU Lightning Complex https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2020/8/16/czu-lightning-complex-including-warnella-fire/. At the end of August the fire had burned 84,640 acres, destroyed over 1100 buildings some of which were residential structures, injured three people (first responders), and killed another. Nearly 100,000 people were forced to evacuate. Historic Big Basin State Park sustained heavy damage from the fire burning down the parks headquarters. The fire was still actively burning at the end of August.

A second round of thunderstorms moved through the region into the morning of August 17th producing additional lightning strikes over the Bay Area. On the early morning of the 17th lightning produced a fire in Napa County that became the Hennessey Fire. Eventually, this fire merged with several other fires across Napa, Sonoma, Solano, Yolo, and Lake Counties (Gamble, 15-10, Spanish, Markley, 13-4, 11-16, Walbridge) to form the LNU Lightning Complex https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2020/8/17/lnu-lightning-complex-includes-hennessey-gamble-15-10-spanish-markley-13-4-11-16-walbridge/. Over 350,000 acres burned with over 200 structures damaged and over 1400 destroyed along with 5 fatalities (3 in Napa County and 2 in Solano County) including civilian and fire personnel across all counties. The LNU Lightning Complex Fire is now one of the top 5 largest wildfires in California state history. The fire was still burning at the end of August.

events.event_narrative: After multiple lightning strikes across the region and breezy erratic winds, approximately 20 separate fires broke out across counties (Santa Clara, Alameda, Contra Costa, San Joaquin, and Stanislaus) the morning of August 16th. These fires were later re-named the SCU Lightning Complex Fires https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2020/8/18/scu-lightning-complex/. This complex became one of the top 5 largest fires in California State history prompting numerous evacuations, destroying nearly 400,000 acres and destroying over 200 structures. These fires resulted in 6 injuries (Civilian and Fire Personnel). The fires came dangerously close to the historic Lick Observatory on Mount Hamilton https://arstechnica.com/science/2020/08/a-california-wildfire-nearly-destroyed-the-historic-lick-observatory/. The fire was still burning at the end of August.

Over 50,000 acres burned by the end of the month along with nearly 80 residential structures and numerous additional structures. Strong and dry offshore winds enabled the Glass Fire to grow nearly fourfold in just one day https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-09-29/glass-fire-quadruples-in-size-burning-80-homes-in-napa-valley. Over 15 inches of rain fell near the area contributing to a large section of Highway 1 collapsing into the Pacific Ocean later that day. Exact cost of repairs is unknown, the section of highway will likely remain closed for months https://www.kron4.com/news/california/when-hwy-1-collapses-by-big-sur-caltrans-engineers-face-unique-challenges/.

At the mouth of the Carmel River a sandbar blocked off the Carmel River Lagoon. Persistent heavy rain sent water into low-lying areas just north of the lagoon with flooding reported at homes on 16th street. The lagoon breached the sandbar by 11 am https://www.ksbw.com/article/californias-covid-19-death-toll-edges-past-new-york/35481836.

A mudslide occurred in the Aptos Hills on Valencia School Rd around midnight. A 50 foot section of a rain soaked roadway gave way and a PG&E rig fell about 150 feet down the hillside https://www.ksbw.com/article/santa-cruz-utility-worker-tumbles-down-150-foot-hillside-during-landslide/35369366.

A mudslide occurred in the Aptos Hills Area causing damage to a home. A truck was pushed into an additional structure. Exact time and location of the slide is unknown https://www.ksbw.com/article/mother-newborn-escape-mudslide-in-aptos-hills/35369344.

Large swell capsized several small boats near the Santa Cruz Harbor in the Monterey Bay Sunday afternoon. Twelve children part of a sail school needed to be rescued after sailboats were capsized. Patrols were already posted in the water and everyone was quickly rescued https://sanfrancisco.cbslocal.com/2021/01/10/massive-swells-capsize-sailboats-at-mouth-of-santa-cruz-harbor-12-children-rescued-from-turbulent-seas/.

On the first day of the month a brush fire broke out in Marin County later named the Lassen Fire. Breezy onshore winds that day as well as prolonged dry conditions helped the fire quickly grow in its early stages. The fire near a populated area with evacuation orders and warnings initially issued. The fire was contained at 44 acres with no structures damaged and no injuries https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2021/9/1/lassen-fire/.

Prolonged region wide dry conditions along with locally breezy winds allowed the Fremont Fire to break out along the Napa/Sonoma County border. No evacuations were needed and no structures were damaged or destroyed https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2021/9/22/fremont-fire/.

events.event_narrative: Strong offshore winds led to a 687 acre fire (Colorado Fire) in Palo Colorado Canyon, sparked by an uncontrolled pile burn. One yurt was damaged and about 500 people were evacuated from about 1100 structures. The fire spread from the canyon down to Highway 1 near the Bixby Creek Bridge, causing a 21 mile section of the highway to be shut down for over a week (between the entrance to Andrew Molera Park in Big Sur to Rio Road in Carmel). No injuries or fatalities were reported. The fire was 100 percent contained on Feb 5th.

A fire started at Geyser Peak early Saturday morning, and grew to about 5 acres before fire crews were able to get it contained. Reports say that the fire initially started at about 1:40am pushed by strong winds, and wind gusts up to 90 miles per hour. An additional smaller fire was reported in the 15000 block of Chalk Hill Road at about 7am, but that fire has also been contained. There were no evacuations for either fire. Power outages were reported in large parts of Sonoma County, including along Chalk Hill Road, in the hills around the Geysers, and along Highway 12 from Glen Ellen to Boyes Hot Springs, as well as to the east of the Town of Sonoma.  As of 7:30am, about 6,700 customers were without power.
